after.title: Preprint: Excluded causal variants produce false discoveries in genetic fine-mapping
after.authors: Weinstock, J. S.
after.abstract: Statistical fine-mapping seeks to distinguish causal genetic variants from correlated variants in linkage disequilibrium (LD). Although fine-mapping algorithms perform well in simulations, they are often applied in settings that violate their assumptions. In particular, genome-wide association study (GWAS) and quantitative trait locus (QTL) workflows routinely omit variants with minor allele frequency (MAF) below 1% and most insertions and deletions (indels), excluding many causal variants before fine-mapping begins. To assess this empirically, we compared filtered and unfiltered fine-mapping at 499 All of Us loci. Twenty percent of high-confidence calls after a 1% MAF filter, and 32% when indels were also omitted, lacked support in the unfiltered analysis. Errors were particularly enriched when tested variants tagged an omitted variant, so fine-mapping misassigned its signal to a proxy variant. At ABO, omitting the frameshift that defines blood group O gave near-certain posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs) to linked single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). To address this disconnect, we developed SuSiE-OUT, which enables fine-mapping in scenarios with possibly omitted causal variants. Modeling infinitesimal effects did not reliably prevent these errors, whereas imputing omitted variants or modeling them with our SuSiE-OUT method prevented most errors. Overall, we find that common analysis workflows substantially increase false discoveries in fine-mapping analyses, and we demonstrate two approaches to mitigate this challenge.

after.title: Preprint: Near-infrared spectroscopy reveals asymmetric hemispheric blood supply during aortic arch surgery
after.authors: El Mokhtari, Y.; Schumacher, F. K.; Podlasek, J.; Meissner, F.; Hiller, A.; Damjanovic, D.; Humburger, F.; Brizzi, F.; Kirr, H.; Berger, T.; Kreibich, M.; Maier, S.; Schimmel, M.; Gottardi, R.; Urbach, H.; Unterrainer, J. M.; Czerny, M.; Kondov, S.; Kaller, C. P.
after.abstract: Objectives: Bilateral and trilateral selective antegrade cerebral perfusion (SACP) aim to ensure symmetric hemispheric perfusion during aortic arch surgery, which current monitoring cannot directly assess. As a step towards real-time monitoring, we assessed the feasibility of multichannel contrast-enhanced near-infrared spectroscopy (CE-NIRS) using indocyanine green and whether hemispheric bolus timing matched expectations for each perfusion configuration. Methods: In this prospective, offline-analysed pilot study, 10 patients undergoing aortic arch surgery (9 frozen elephant trunk) received 94 boluses across 10 perfusion configurations. The interhemispheric difference in time to peak ({Delta}TTP) was compared with the pre-bypass baseline using a linear mixed model with Holm correction, alongside cerebral oximetry; the relationship to postoperative cerebral injury was explored post hoc. Results: 92 of 94 boluses yielded a bilateral TTP. Contrary to expectation, the left hemisphere peaked later under bilateral (+7.2 s, 95% CI 3.4-11.0; p = 0.003) and trilateral SACP (+8.7 s, 2.5-14.8; p = 0.031). With both left-sided arch vessels on body perfusion, the asymmetry reversed (-7.0 s, -11.7 to -2.3; p = 0.025). {Delta}TTP detected 6 of 9 configuration effects, whereas oximetry detected none after correction. The three patients with cerebral injury showed the three most pronounced reversals (exact p = 0.100) but were also those managed trilaterally. Conclusions: Multichannel CE-NIRS is feasible during aortic arch surgery, without indicator-related adverse events. Bilateral and trilateral SACP did not secure symmetric indicator delivery; the configuration-dependent asymmetry and its reversal point to two steals within the perfusion circuit that oximetry missed. Their clinical relevance requires prospective confirmation.

after.title: Preprint: Dengue among febrile patients in Ghana: prevalence and facility-level variation in a multisite surveillance study
after.authors: Zigah, F.; Agyei-Nkansah, A. A.; Tagoe, E. A.; Gyapon, I. A. T.; Bonney, K.; Adomako-Boateng, F.; Punguyire, D. T.; Oliver-Commey, J. A.; Adzesi, R. S.; Sagoe, K. W. C.; Afrane, Y. A.; Pappoe-Ashong, P. J. P.-A. J.; Kenu, E.; Grobbee, D. E.; van der Sande, M. A. B.
after.abstract: Introduction: Dengue is under-recognized in Ghana, where laboratory testing is limited. We estimated dengue NS1 and/or IgM positivity among febrile patients and described geographical, temporal, and demographic variation. Methodology: We conducted cross-sectional surveillance among consenting febrile patients aged [≥]1 year at six public facilities in Greater Accra, Bono East, and Upper West between August 2023 and July 2025. We randomly selected one region within each of three ecological strata and selected facilities with high febrile-case volumes. We approached and recruited consecutive eligible patients. We tested serum for dengue NS1 antigen and IgM antibody by ELISA; positive NS1 samples underwent RT-PCR and serotyping. We estimated proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and used logistic regression to examine adjusted associations. Results: Among 2,936 participants, 204 were NS1- and/or IgM-positive (6.95%; 95% CI, 6.05-7.93%): 31 were NS1-only, 161 IgM-only, and 12 dual-positive. Prevalence ranged from 3.88% (95% CI, 2.19-6.31%) at Kintampo to 12.32% (9.56-15.55%) at Atebubu, both in Bono East. Adjusted odds increased with age (aOR per five years, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.05-1.14). Eight of 43 NS1-positive samples contained dengue RNA: five DENV-1 from Bono East and three DENV-3 from Upper West. There was no clear rainy-dry season difference. Conclusions: Dengue NS1 and/or IgM were detected among febrile patients at all six facilities, and RT-PCR confirmed circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-3. These findings support including dengue in febrile illness evaluation and strengthening laboratory-supported surveillance in Ghana. Keywords: dengue, febrile illness, NS1 antigen, IgM, DENV-1, DENV-3, Ghana

after.title: Preprint: Reconstructing age-specific social contact patterns across 28 EU/EEA countries during the COVID-19 pandemic: linking non-pharmaceutical interventions to social mixing, 2020-2022
after.authors: Chatzilena, A.; Brooks-Pollock, E.; Colman, E.; Hansson, D.; Demiris, N.; Franklin, B.; Danon, L.
after.abstract: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, most EU/EEA countries sequentially introduced non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) to reduce social contacts and mitigate transmission. The CoMix study captured real-time changes in social mixing, but substantial spatiotemporal gaps remain, with some countries lacking pandemic contact data. We developed a model-based framework to estimate time-varying changes in age-specific contact patterns and relate these changes to NPIs recorded in the ECDC-JRC Response Measures Database. This relationship was used to predict contacts during periods without CoMix observations. For countries without CoMix data, we reconstructed temporal age-specific mixing patterns using estimates from countries with pandemic contact data selected through a country-matching process based on socio-demographic characteristics and similarity in NPI implementation. We generated age-specific contact matrices for 28 EU/EEA countries spanning 2020-2022. Reconstructed patterns captured substantial temporal and cross-country variation in social mixing and its evolving association with NPIs across diverse European contexts. Our framework provides estimates that extend incomplete pandemic contact data across both time and countries, yielding a consistent set of age-specific contact matrices for the EU/EEA. These estimates address important gaps in empirical social-contact data and provide valuable insights into the interplay of NPIs and social mixing patterns which is of critical importance to improving epidemic modelling and policy making.

after.title: Preprint: Effect of starting metformin on severe and long COVID-19 among people living with type 2 diabetes in England: a new user cohort study in OpenSAFELY-TPP
after.authors: Amstutz, A.; Walker, V.; Madley-Dowd, P.; Denholm, R.; Zou, M.; Palmer, T. M.; OpenSAFELY Collaborative,  ; Eastwood, S. V.; Hulme, W. J.; Sterne, J. A. C.
after.abstract: Introduction: Observational studies report lower COVID-19 mortality among metformin users, but most used prevalent-user designs comparing long-term survivors with heterogeneous controls. Randomised trials suggest little or no mortality effect. No large observational study has used a new-user design to estimate the effect of starting versus not starting metformin on severe and Long COVID outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). We aimed to estimate this effect on COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, COVID-19 diagnoses, and Long COVID among adults with T2D in England. Research design and methods: Using OpenSAFELY-TPP linked NHS electronic health records, we conducted a population-based cohort study with a landmark new-user design. Adults aged 18-85 years newly diagnosed with T2D (August 2018-August 2019) were classified as starting metformin monotherapy within 6 months or not starting any antidiabetic drug, based on prescription data. Follow-up began 6 months after diagnosis and before the UK pandemic (avoiding immortal time) for up to 2 years. We estimated intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects using weighted Cox and pooled logistic regression, with negative (bone fracture) and positive (diabetes-related death) control outcomes. Results: Of 52,341 eligible people, 19,599 (37.4%) started metformin. For COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, the maximally adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of metformin versus no antidiabetic was 1.17 (95% CI 1.02-1.35; 2-year risk difference 0.36%, 95% CI 0.09-0.62; intention-to-treat). The per-protocol HR for COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death was 1.11 (95% CI 0.96-1.29). The Long COVID estimate was imprecise (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.83-2.33; intention-to-treat). For bone fracture (negative control) the estimate was null (HR 1.00), but for diabetes-related deaths (positive control) it was elevated (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.09-1.81), indicating unmeasured confounding. Conclusions: The risks of severe and long COVID were slightly higher among people who started metformin, compared with those who did not start. These results plausibly reflect unmeasured confounding. These findings align more closely with randomised evidence than earlier prevalent-user studies and argue against a clinically meaningful benefit of starting metformin for COVID-19 prevention in newly diagnosed T2D.

after.title: Preprint: Lipidome-wide analysis of concurrent and longitudinal blood pressure patterns in school-aged children
after.authors: ALFANO, R.; nawrot, t.; barth, k.; giesberts, n.; renaers, e.; vangeneugden, m.; Plusquin, M.
after.abstract: Background: Elevated blood pressure (BP) in childhood is associated with cardiovascular risk, but its molecular lipid correlates remain poorly characterized. We investigated the association of plasma lipid species and patterns with concurrent and longitudinal BP phenotypes in school-aged children. Methods: In the Belgian ENVIRONAGE prospective birth-cohort, 195 children aged 9 to 12 years were examined between July 2021 and September 2024. A total of 1,232 plasma lipid species were quantified using liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations with systolic and diastolic BP percentiles were examined using multivariable linear regression with permutation-based family-wise error rate (FWER) correction. Lipid-set enrichment analysis, with P values from sample permutation to account for correlation among lipid species, evaluated coordinated associations. Significant findings were examined across longitudinal BP patterns in 177 children with BP measured at ages 4-6 and 9-12. Findings: Each 1-SD increase in triglyceride (TG) 58:9 fatty acyl (FA) 22:4 was associated with 7.36 higher systolic BP percentile points (95% CI=3.91-10.80; P_FWER=0.03). TG 58:9 FA 22:4 was associated with incident (OR=2.78; 95% CI=1.33-5.79) and persistent (OR=2.14; 95% CI=1.22-3.77), but not resolved elevated BP vs stable-normal BP. Among lipid sets, species with a total carbon number of 38, mainly PC and PE, were inversely enriched with diastolic BP percentile. Interpretation: Childhood BP was associated with higher levels of a highly polyunsaturated long-chain TG, closely related to current BP elevation and not elevated among children whose BP had normalized.

after.authors: Erb, A.; Misciagna, A.; Rodriguez-Martinez, A.; Gasser, B.; DeFilippo, C.; Gillam, A.; Beleford, D.; VanNoy, G.; Young-Baird, S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Uniformed Services University, Bethesda, MD 20814
after.abstract: The translation initiation factor eIF2 is an essential regulator of cellular protein synthesis with direct links to human physiology and development. Composed of eIF2, {beta}, and {gamma} subunits, eIF2 heterotrimer assembly requires the activity of its dedicated chaperone and the essential protein, CDC123. Accordingly, CDC123 is a key determinant of protein synthesis and cell growth. Previous research has demonstrated that variants in eIF2{gamma} impair neurodevelopment, and CDC123 variants of uncertain significance have recently been reported for pediatric patients with neurologic findings. However, the potential pathogenicity, and cell and molecular impacts of these clinically relevant CDC123 variants remains entirely unexplored. In this work, we describe four unrelated families with pediatric patients that present with neurodevelopmental delays, hypotonia, and motor dysfunction. The probands are heterozygous for three novel CDC123 missense variants. The potential pathogenicity of the variants is comprehensively assessed through appraisal of CDC123 variant allele frequencies, protein conservational analyses, structural modeling, and functional assays in both humanized yeast and human cell-based model systems. Cellular and biochemical studies indicated that the variants are damaging to CDC123 activity, altering CDC123-eIF2 subunit interactions and leading to reduced cell growth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the CDC123 variants display dominant-negative effects on yeast cell growth and protein synthesis, rather than causing haploinsufficiency. Together, our findings provide the first link between CDC123 missense variants and human disease and highlight that CDC123-mediated eIF2 heterotrimer formation is essential for human development.

Instead, they form a highly correlated 'exposome' whose multidimensional relationships with brain development and behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Elucidating the complex interplay between brain, behavior, and environment requires a multivariate approach. This study used regularized multiset canonical correlation analysis on longitudinal data from 8,113 preadolescents in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study to characterize latent multivariate dimensions linking diverse environmental exposures, tract-wisely resolved measures of white matter (WM) development and integrity, and multi-domain behavioral phenotypes and relate them to concurrent and future psychopathology. Two distinct multivariate dimensions were identified exhibiting different exposure, WM development, and behavior patterns. The first linked greater socioeconomic resources to more advanced WM development, particularly in dorsal-association tracts, and superior cognitive performance. The second dimension linked stronger psychosocial support with higher WM integrity, more advanced development of limbic tracts, and lower levels of psychopathology. Longitudinal analyses revealed differential contributions of these dimensions to follow-up cognitive, socioemotional and psychiatric outcomes. Moreover, WM and exposomic variates in these dimensions moderated the effects of childhood adversity on transdiagnostic psychiatric disorder risk, in sex- and context-specific fashions. Together, these findings clarify how childhood environmental exposures and the linked WM developmental differences relate to cognition and psychopathology risk, potentially informing the identification of candidate neural targets for future interventions.

after.authors: Riepenhausen, A.; Jacob, G. A.; Probst, T.; Klein, J. P.
after.abstract: The digital therapeutic priovi has small average effects for borderline personality disorder (BPD). In this preregistered secondary analysis, we aimed to explore the heterogeneity and potential moderators of these effects. Adults received priovi plus treatment as usual or treatment as usual alone. At the 3-month primary endpoint (N = 528), model-based recursive partitioning showed heterogeneous effects on Borderline Symptom List-23 (BSL-23) change (p = 0.022) and on clinically relevant response (p = 0.007). Benefit was larger at higher baseline symptom load: a representative tree split on Patient Health Questionnaire-9 at a score of 23, and the higher-score subgroup had roughly twice the BSL-23 reduction (conditional average treatment effects -0.40 versus -0.19). Baseline BSL-23, depressive symptoms, and recent life-threatening events ranked as the leading moderators. Quartile calibration of predicted CATEs was weak and non-monotonic. The moderators are hypothesis-generating and should not guide patient selection without external validation.

after.authors: Souza, B. R.; Guimaraes, J. S. d. F.; de Assis, M. M. R.; de Souza, E. M. S.; Fonseca, L. R. A.; Pires, A. C. V.; de Carvalho, I. R.; dos Anjos, K. C. C.; Nascimento, M. A. d. C.; Lima, M. C. S. B.; Castro, M. C. D.; Ferreira, M. E. M. d. A.; Mansur, V. F.; Oliveira, A. G.
after.abstract: The rapid expansion of online gambling and sports betting has raised concerns about gambling-related harm and its implications for public health. However, nationwide evidence regarding temporal trends and patterns of health care utilization associated with gambling remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. We conducted a nationwide retrospective study using administrative data from Brazil's Unified Health System from 2014 through 2025. We examined primary health care records associated with pathological gambling (ICD-10, code F63.0) and gambling and betting (code Z72.6). We analyzed temporal trends, seasonal patterns, and geographic and demographic distributions, calculating annual encounter rates per 100,000 inhabitants. Gambling-related primary health care encounters increased substantially during the study period, with a marked acceleration beginning in 2022. By 2025, nationwide rates reached 1.46 encounters per 100,000 inhabitants for pathological gambling and 0.60 per 100,000 for gambling and betting. Increases were observed across all five Brazilian regions, with the highest rates in the South and Southeast. Recorded encounters increased across age groups and both sexes, particularly among adults aged 20 to 39 years. Rates were also elevated among adolescent males and older women. Time-series analyses suggested seasonal variation, with higher indices generally between April and October. Gambling-related encounters in Brazilian primary health care increased markedly from 2014 through 2025, particularly after 2022, with substantial demographic and geographic variation. These findings indicate increasing documentation of gambling-related conditions within a nationwide public health system and underscore the need for improved surveillance, early identification, and access to appropriate mental health care.

after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Vermont College of Medicine
after.abstract: Abstract Background and Objective: Pediatric emergency department (ED) visits for suicidal ideation and behavior have increased substantially, highlighting the need for scalable outpatient interventions that reduce recurrent ED use. We tested whether referral to outpatient crisis services was associated with fewer mental health-related ED revisits, hypothesizing that referred youth would have lower revisit rates than those receiving usual community care. Methods: We conducted a quasi-experimental study of 3,125 youth presenting with suicidal ideation or behavior to a large academic childrens health system between October 1, 2023, and August 31, 2025. Youth were referred to outpatient crisis services or community treatment (usual care) based on slot availability and clinician discretion. Propensity score modeling balanced demographic, clinical, and prior treatment characteristics between groups. Results: Among 3,125 qualifying index ED visits, 763 (24.4%) youth were referred to crisis services and 461 (14.8%) received [≥]1 crisis visit within 30 days. In intent-to-treat analyses, referral was associated with fewer mental health-related ED revisits at 90 days (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR], 0.67; 95% CI, 0.56-0.81) and 180 days (aIRR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.59-0.80). Associations were strongest among youth requiring short-term hospitalization (aIRR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and those with moderate-to-high suicide risk (aIRR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39-0.61). Findings were consistent in as-treated analyses. Conclusion: Outpatient crisis services were associated with substantially fewer mental health-related ED revisits among suicidal youth, with the largest reductions among youth with greater clinical acuity.

after.abstract: Objective: Schizophrenia (SZ) and bipolar disorder (BP) emerge in late adolescence or adulthood. Offspring at familial high risk for SZ (FHR-SZ) or BP (FHR-BP) are more likely to develop psychiatric disorders. Prior work from the Danish High Risk and Resilience (VIA) Study found sex-specific volumetric brain differences in offspring at FHR-SZ and FHR-BP aged 11-12 years. This study builds upon these findings by testing whether they reflect group differences in rate of change or stable group differences from early to mid-adolescence. Methods: This study investigated MRI data from offspring at FHR-SZ, FHR-BP, and population- based controls (PBC) at baseline (11-12 years; n=288) and follow-up (15-16 years; n=249). FreeSurfer longitudinal processing derived total brain volume, cortical measures, and intracranial volume (ICV). Linear mixed-effects models tested group-by-age interactions and sex-specific group effects, as well as associations with psychotic experiences (PE) and lifetime Axis-I mental disorders. Results: The analysis did not detect group-by-age interactions, indicating similar developmental slopes across groups. However, at both time points, males at FHR-SZ demonstrated reduced brain and cortical volumes compared to PBC and FHR-BP males. These effects were attenuated after adjusting for ICV, which was reduced in males at FHR-SZ. The analysis additionally detected volumetric reductions in males with PE, after controlling for risk status. Conclusions: These results extend the previous findings to ages 15-16 years, indicating group differences are stable and persist into mid-adolescence. Associations with ICV suggest early neurodevelopmental effects, and volumetric reductions in males with PE suggest convergent effects with FHR-SZ.

after.abstract: Reduced-dose pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) schedules (1+1; one primary and one booster) are now endorsed by the World Health Organisation under specific circumstances. Serotype-specific memory B cells (BMEM) are a marker of long-term protection but data from infant reduced-dose trials remain limited. As part of a randomised controlled trial in Vietnamese infants, we characterised serotype-specific BMEM responses in randomised subsets (N=50 per vaccine group per timepoint) following 0+1 (at 12 months of age) or 1+1 (2 and 12 months of age) schedules of PCV10 or PCV13, using a multimer spectral flow cytometry approach. Blood samples were collected at 12 months of age (baseline) and at day 7 and day 28 post-vaccination. A one or two dose schedule of either PCV induced robust serotype-specific BMEM responses at day 7 and day 28 for most serotypes. PCV13 generated earlier and higher BMEM responses than PCV10, while 1+1 schedules for either PCV produced higher BMEM responses than the 0+1 schedules at day 7. By day 28, these differences between the 0+1 and 1+1 schedules were no longer apparent. Notably, BMEM responses for serotypes 6B and 23F were detectable even in infants who did not achieve protective levels of serotype-specific IgG greater or equal to 0.35 ug/mL. PCV13 generated higher plasmablast and plasma cell responses by day 7, and higher cTfh responses by day 28, compared to PCV10. These findings show that 1+1 schedules of PCV10 or PCV13 induce robust BMEM responses, with important implications for the evaluation of PCVs and understanding long-term protection.

after.title: Preprint: Displaced by a Volcano: Adolescent Well-Being in Uncertain Times in Iceland 2023-2026
after.authors: Reimer, D.; Repo, J.; Kilpi-Jakonen, E.; Palsdottir, K.
after.abstract: Aims: The November 2023 evacuation of Grindavik, Iceland, left families facing prolonged uncertainty about return. We examined adolescent well-being before and after evacuation and changes in gaps with national peers between 2025 and 2026. Methods: Repeated cross-sectional analyses used the 2023, 2025, and 2026 Icelandic Youth Study waves, adjusting for grade, gender, and non-Icelandic background. The town's single school in 2023 provided the pre-evacuation benchmark, with models accounting for national time trends. Adolescents who moved before evacuation provided a mobility benchmark. Results: In 2025, evacuees reported lower life satisfaction and school belonging, more psychosomatic symptoms, and higher odds of school absence and past-30-day substance use than the national reference group. The three well-being outcomes departed from the pre-evacuation pattern. Life-satisfaction and belonging gaps were larger among girls than boys in 2025, but these gender differences narrowed by 2026. Comparisons with prior movers suggested a distinct evacuation-related pattern in 2025 among evacuee girls, who reported lower life satisfaction and school belonging than prior-mover girls. In 2026, psychosomatic symptoms (B = 0.29, 95% CI [0.08, 0.49]), absenteeism (OR = 1.81, 95% CI [1.26, 2.60]), and substance use (OR = 2.59, 95% CI [1.75, 3.84]) remained higher relative to the national reference group. Life satisfaction and belonging were directionally lower, with intervals including zero. Change estimates did not establish narrowing of the gaps. Conclusions: The findings underscore the need for sustained educational and well-being support to address adolescents' social connections alongside their mental health during prolonged displacement, including in a Nordic welfare setting.

after.title: Preprint: Age-related Trust and its Association with Cost-related Medication Nonadherence
after.authors: Zhang, J. X.; Meltzer, D.
after.abstract: Trust operates foundationally at the personal and societal levels, a vital force that drives social connection, cooperation, and positive outcomes. In healthcare, trust is instrumental in improving patient outcomes as it forms the foundation for shared decision-making and patient-provider relationships. With growing evidence that generalized trust toward other people grows with age and behaviors such as cost-related medication non-adherence (CRN) decrease with age we study whether lack of trust is a force that drives up CRN and its variability in effects across age groups, controlling for other risk factors. The data consists of 680 Medicare diabetes patients at high risk of hospitalization enrolled in a randomized controlled trial of the effect of the Comprehensive Care Physician model (CCP) at an academic medical center between November 2012 and June 2016. This study provides first-of-its-kind evidence that lack of trust is an important force that drives up CRN and the effect of lack of trust decreased even though the lack of trust decreased by age increments. The effect of lack of trust is particularly pronounced among younger patients. For practice and policy, it shows the potential promising prospect that a more trusting attitude may be conducive to more productive health. More research is needed on how to build trust at the societal level and in healthcare specifically, and how generalized trust and target-specific trust of providers are correlated.

after.abstract: In this study, LLM and prompting strategies for labeling Specific Incidental Findings (SIFs) occurring during lung cancer screening, in radiology reports were compared. In this retrospective study, 300 CT reports from a Dutch academic hospital were included between 19th March 2003 and 28th December 2020. GPT-5, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B-INST, MedGemma-4B-IT, a keyword-based search method, and a radiologist labelled the reports for the presence or absence of nine SIFs. The radiologist's scores were the reference standard. after.title: Preprint: WALRUS: Robust and Transferable Deep Learning for Water and Lipid Removal in 1H-MRSI
after.authors: Fischer, H.; Motyka, S.; Weiser, P.; Strasser, B.; Hingerl, L.; Eckstein, K.; Chaknam, K.; Osburg, A. P.; Altmeyer, A.; Campilho, B.; Sazonova, E.; Li, Y.; Liu, J.; Dymerska, B.; Eftekhari, Z.; Shaw, T. B.; Barth, M.; Hangel, G.; Kaushik, S.; Haider, L.; Bogner, W.
after.abstract: Proton magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (1H-MRSI) enables non-invasive mapping of brain metabolism, but reliable quantification is challenged by residual water and extracranial lipid contamination. Recent work demonstrated that a deep learning model trained on simulated metabolite spectra combined with in vivo-derived water and lipid signals can outperform conventional nuisance-removal methods. However, this approach relied on heuristic simulation parameter distributions and a subject-specific L2-derived lipid estimate as an auxiliary network input, requiring subject-specific lipid masks and L2 processing during inference. Here, we introduce WALRUS (Water And Lipid Removal Using Spectral Learning), a fitting-consistent and empirically calibrated framework developed through a systematic evaluation of simulation realism, architectural priors, and network optimization. WALRUS uses the same metabolite basis as downstream spectral fitting and calibrates deliberately broadened simulation distributions from in vivo measurements. Controlled 7 T experiments demonstrate that empirical simulator calibration substantially improves nuisance removal and metabolite quantification compared with heuristic training distributions. With the optimized simulator, a capacity-matched comparison reveals no clear additional benefit from the L2-derived prior, allowing its removal and substantially simplifying inference. Further improvements are achieved with the final higher-capacity U-Net, while on-the-fly simulation improves generalization compared with training on a fixed synthetic dataset. The same framework was subsequently recalibrated and retrained at 3 T, where WALRUS outperformed conventional HLSVD+L2 processing on held-out data. Together, WALRUS combines these advances into an optimized framework that improves nuisance removal and downstream metabolite fitting, requires no subject-specific lipid segmentation or L2-derived auxiliary input during inference, and can be systematically adapted to different acquisition settings.

after.abstract: Background: The Lung-RADS algorithm standardizes the management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules, but its risk assessment is driven chiefly by nodule size and attenuation. This misallocates a meaningful fraction of patients: a nontrivial share of small malignancies receive 12-month surveillance while large benign nodules proceed to invasive workup. Artificial intelligence (AI) may supply risk information independent of the imaging features Lung-RADS already uses. Methods: We validated LungAI, an investigational deep learning nodule malignancy classifier not yet cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), on the held-out NLST test partition of Ardila et al. (2,747 low-dose CT examinations from 1,244 patients with at least 1 solid or part-solid 4-30 mm nodule; 89 pathologically confirmed cancers, prevalence 3.2%). We compared discrimination against Sybil, mean nodule diameter, and estimated nodule volume. A board-certified radiologist assigned Lung-RADS v2022 categories to a positives-enriched random subset (226 eligible examinations; 78 cancers), projected to the full cohort by contingency weighting. A per-category reclassification algorithm shifted patients along the existing Lung-RADS management ladder using a-priori score cutpoints. We evaluated a separately locked follow-up configuration on examinations with a prior scan. Results: LungAI achieved AUROC 0.92 (95% CI 0.88-0.95) and AUPRC 0.47 (0.35-0.61), outperforming Sybil (delta AUROC 0.07; delta AUPRC 0.18), diameter (delta AUROC 0.14; delta AUPRC 0.34), and volume (delta AUROC 0.14; delta AUPRC 0.38; all P<0.001). Against Lung-RADS v2022 scored ordinally on the weighted annotated subset, LungAI improved AUPRC (delta AUPRC 0.31, P=0.003) but not AUROC (delta AUROC 0.03, P=0.20). LungAI added discriminative information independent of diameter (likelihood-ratio chi squared = 161, P < 10e-36; delta AUROC 0.10) and, on follow-up examinations, independent of delta diameter, volume doubling time, and new-nodule status (chi squared = 79, P < 10e-18). Integrated with Lung-RADS, LungAI reduced cancers on the slowest (12-month rescan) pathway by 46% (3.1 --> 1.6 per 1,000 examinations) and benign biopsy referrals by 20% (32.7 --> 26.2 per 1,000 examinations) at approximately unchanged total biopsy volume (51.0 --> 50.1 per 1,000). Assuming full adherence to recommended follow-up, the combined approach yielded 25 months of net diagnostic lead time, an estimated net cost saving of ~$2,200, and 6.5 fewer benign biopsies per 1,000 examinations; accounting for published adherence rates, it yielded 1.6 additional cancer diagnoses within 1 year per 1,000 examinations. Conclusions: LungAI contributes malignancy-risk information orthogonal to the size- and growth-based features underlying Lung-RADS and improves the allocation of screening patients across the existing management spectrum while potentially decreasing invasive procedures for benign lesions. Multi-site, multi-geography validation is required to demonstrate practical generalizability.

after.title: Preprint: Five Days of Acute Intermittent Hypoxia Is Safe and Improves Somatic Motor Function in Persons with Multiple Sclerosis
after.authors: Nehrujee, A.; Kalvakota, R.; Barry, A.; O'Shea, L.; Johnson, H. R.; Zou, C.; Northrop, J. N.; Mannella, K.; Dee, W.; Rymer, W. Z.; Nemeth, A. J.; Cohen, B. A.; Bright, M. G.; Sandhu, M. S.
after.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES Walking impairment affects up to 75% of persons with multiple sclerosis (MS), and the benefits of rehabilitation are constrained by limited capacity for training-induced neuroplasticity. Acute intermittent hypoxia (AIH), brief repeated exposures to low inspired oxygen, triggers serotonin-dependent spinal plasticity that enhances motor output. In spinal cord injury, daily AIH paired with walking training has produced larger walking gains than training alone, positioning AIH as a promising primer for rehabilitation. Before AIH can be combined with training in MS, its safety and stand-alone effects with repeated daily dosing must be established in a population with demyelinating disease. We therefore conducted the first multi-day AIH trial in persons with MS to characterize safety and tolerability and to evaluate preliminary effects on ankle strength and walking. METHODS Twenty-three ambulatory adults with MS (Expanded Disability Status Scale [EDSS] 3.0-6.5; 15 relapsing-remitting, 8 secondary-progressive) completed a randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Participants received AIH (15 x ~60 s episodes; FiO2 = 0.09; SpO2 target 84-88%) and Sham in a counterbalanced order, separated by a washout of at least 4 weeks. Assessments at pre-intervention, post-intervention, and follow-up included ankle plantarflexion and dorsiflexion torque, 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), Timed 25-Foot Walk (T25FW), and MS Walking Scale-12 (MSWS-12). Treatment effects were estimated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with participant as a random effect. RESULTS No serious adverse events related to the intervention were reported, and follow-up MRI showed no new MS activity in either arm. Mean nadir SpO2 during AIH was 84.7 +/- 0.2%, and cardiovascular parameters returned to baseline within minutes of each session completion. Ankle plantarflexion torque was significantly greater following AIH than Sham (beta = 8.74 Nm, p < 0.001), with mean increases of 17.5% at post-intervention and 29.2% at follow-up. Six-minute walk distance was also significantly greater after AIH (beta = 10.14 m, p = 0.039). Dorsiflexion torque (p = 0.202), T25FW time (p = 0.239), and MSWS-12 score (p = 0.564) did not differ significantly between conditions. Greater elevation in heart rate during hypoxic episodes was associated with larger strength gains at follow-up (r = 0.58, p = 0.009). CONCLUSIONS: Daily AIH sessions are safe and well tolerated in persons with MS across a clinically heterogeneous disability range and produce significant improvements in ankle plantarflexion strength and walking endurance. These findings support combining AIH with task-specific gait training in future trials.

after.authors: Sjodin, E. M.; Chasman, D. I.; Chen, M.-H.; Rist, P. M.; Johnson, A. D.
after.abstract: Objective We assessed potential associations between migraine and complete blood cell count (CBC) data in three large population-based studies. Background Platelets are thought to be involved in migraine pathology through increased activation during an attack. Migraine attacks are often treated with NSAIDs that inhibit platelets, or triptans that target serotonin receptors, with serotonin being most highly expressed in circulation within platelet granules. However, the exact role of platelets in migraine remains unclear. Methods The UK BioBank (UKBB) has CBC data available from baseline blood samples and migraine diagnoses were obtained through self-report and electronic health records. CBC and migraine data from the 1999-2000, 2001-2002, and 2003-2004 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) study were obtained during single exam visits. CBCs were obtained from Framingham Heart Study (FHS) participants. Migraine history was assessed through clinical diagnostic impressions. The UKBB sample (18,919 cases (4,580 incident); 448,339 controls) was the primary discovery cohort for CBCs, with replication meta-analysis done in NHANES (1,887 cases; 7,242 controls) and FHS (395 cases (229 incident); 3,172 controls). Our primary model adjusted for age and sex, with secondary analysis adjusting for additional factors. Sex-stratified, sex-interaction and ancestry-stratified (UKBB only) analyses were also performed. Results Migraine was associated with platelet count (PLT) in the UKBB (OR=1.058, 95% CI [1.043,1.073], p=2.09E-14) and was replicated in the NHANES-FHS meta-analysis (OR=1.074, 95% CI [1.025,1.126], p=0.003). PLT also drove multiple significant signals of PLT-involved CBC ratios. While neutrophil counts and hemoglobin were associated with migraine in UKBB, these did not replicate in FHS-NHANES meta-analysis. Conclusion Higher platelet count is associated with an increased likelihood of migraine. Further studies with longitudinal assessments of CBCs and migraine attacks are needed to further understand the role of platelets in the onset of migraine attacks.

after.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, noninvasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-beta burden using Cookie Theft picture descriptions from two cohorts of Hebrew- and English-speaking participants (IRAP, N=134; WRAP, N=1,541). after.abstract: Background: Population aging and immunosenescence pose immense challenges to healthcare systems by increasing susceptibility to infections. Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LP28 (L. plantarum LP28) is a strain isolated from traditional Taiwanese dried tofu with significant immunomodulatory potential. Objective: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of long-term L. plantarum LP28 supplementation in common cold prevention and its effect on systemic immune biomarkers in middle-aged and elderly individuals. Methods: In this 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 102 middle-aged and older adults (aged 50-75 years) were assigned to receive an oral probiotic (5 x 109 CFU L. plantarum LP28/capsule, two capsules daily; n = 51) or a placebo (n = 51). Cold incidence and symptom severity were evaluated by the Wisconsin Upper Respiratory Symptom Survey (WURSS). Immune cell populations, serum/salivary markers, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were quantified using flow cytometry, ELISAs and NK cell cytotoxicity assays, respectively. The data were analyzed using a refined per-protocol approach and outlier-removed sensitivity analyses to ensure robustness. Independent t tests, chi-square/Fisher's exact tests, and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for statistical comparisons. Results: The probiotic group exhibited a notable reduction in cold incidence (34.78% vs. 52.00% in the placebo group) and a lower cumulative symptom burden. In terms of immunomodulatory effects, L. plantarum LP28 supplementation significantly increased serum interleukin (IL)-12 levels and NK cell cytotoxicity, reinforcing innate immune defense through the activation of the IL-12/NK cell axis. This was accompanied by a significant reduction in the level of the inflammatory marker C-reactive protein (CRP). Conclusions: L. plantarum LP28 supplementation serves as an effective supportive strategy for promoting healthy aging by increasing respiratory defense resilience and mitigating systemic inflammatory stress through pleiotropic immune modulation.

after.authors: Wood, D. E.; Ballew, B. J.; Roy, J.
after.abstract: Current cancer screening efforts face the dual problems of low patient adherence and a lack of available tests for many cancers, which motivates the development of less invasive multi-cancer early detection strategies. Such strategies will likely involve the use of liquid biopsies, which can analyze biomarkers found in blood for the presence of cancer. We introduce Blackjack, a new detection approach that focuses on the fragmentation patterns of plasma-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Blackjack characterizes a person's cfDNA fragmentation sites with a position probability matrix (PPM) that encodes information about the sequence context of the sites. For classification, Blackjack computes two features that represent the similarity of an individual's PPM to those of known healthy and cancer cohorts. With these two features, Blackjack then uses logistic regression to classify a new sample as being from a healthy individual or a person with cancer. In cross-validation experiments using two external whole genome sequencing datasets, Blackjack showed high performance, achieving a minimum area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.993 and minimum sensitivity (Sn) of 91.8% (at 98% specificity). This high performance was also present for stage I (AUC 0.991, Sn 89.8%) and stage II cancers (AUC 0.993, Sn 90.2%), and across eight different cancers (minimum AUC 0.985, minimum Sn 80.0%). We demonstrate that Blackjack's accuracy is stable at low simulated sequencing depths (~0.24x), and that tissue of origin prediction using Blackjack's similarity measures is high (minimum 82% accuracy of the top two predicted tissues). Our findings show that cfDNA fragmentation site contexts have valuable signals for early cancer detection, and that developing diagnostics with machine learning can benefit from a focus on having a small number of informative features.

after.authors: Sabin, P. M.; Dadvar, F.; Mirville, R.; Nam, Y.; Hamid, F.; Bradley, C.; Yohannan, J.; Clingo, K. A.; Johnson, T. V.; Chiang, B.; Quigley, H. A.; Nguyen, T. D.
after.abstract: Objective: To estimate the lamina cribrosa (LC) strain response to intraocular pressure (IOP) change in open angle glaucoma (OAG) patients and examine associations between LC strain and demographic and clinical characteristics relevant to OAG in an ongoing longitudinal study. Design: Cohort study Participants: Adult patients with OAG (205 eyes of 119 patients) Methods: The STRAIN study is an ongoing longitudinal study designed to determine whether LC biomechanical strain is associated with present, prior, and future OAG damage. In this initial analysis, patients either temporarily stopped [≥] 1 eye drop, initiated an eye drop, or underwent selective laser trabeculoplasty to produce IOP change. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans of the optic nerve head (ONH) acquired before and up to several weeks after IOP change were analyzed using digital volume correlation (DVC) to estimate LC strain. Strain measurements were compared with age, race, sex, axial length, central corneal thickness (CCT), corneal hysteresis, optic disc area, years of known OAG, retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, and visual field mean deviation (MD). Main Outcome Measures: LC strain estimated by DVC from OCT scans acquired before and after IOP alteration. Results: Axial LC strain (Ezz) was tensile with IOP decrease and compressive with IOP increase. Maximum principal strain was tensile (mean Emax = 1.09%), and maximum shear strain was positive (mean{Gamma} max = 1.16%) in the radial-axial plane. Both increased quadratically with the IOP change. Older age was significantly related to greater tensile circumferential strain (p = 0.02) and lower{Gamma} max (p = 0.01). Sex, CCT, corneal hysteresis, and optic disc area were not significantly associated with LC strain. In combined multivariable models adjusting for IOP change, demographics, and accounting for correlations between eyes from the same patient, eyes with thinner inferior-quadrant RNFL had smaller{Gamma} max for a given IOP change (p = 0.02). Conclusions: LC strain in patients with OAG is associated with the degree of neuronal loss, age, and axial length, supporting a relationship between the LC biomechanical response and factors relevant to glaucomatous damage.

after.authors: Sarkar, M. S. S.; Saon, M. T. H.; Basak, S.
after.abstract: In clinical datasets, data augmentation is often avoided because it can remove important unusual values, known as outliers, which are important for understanding diseases accurately. However, clinical EEG datasets often suffer from two key limitations: small sample sizes and class imbalance, which significantly reduce classification performance. To overcome these challenges, this study applies generative AI-based data augmentation techniques with a carefully designed hybrid pipeline that effectively enhances performance even on limited EEG data. Using EEG signals from 50 brain stroke patients, we investigate both traditional oversampling methods (SMOTE and ADASYN) and advanced generative models, including WGAN and WGAN-GP. Our proposed pipeline involves preprocessing EEG recordings, extracting comprehensive statistical and frequency-domain features, applying feature reduction, and evaluating multiple machine learning classifiers. Experimental results show that the combination of SelectKBest feature selection, SVM classifier, and WGAN-GP augmentation achieves the highest classification accuracy of 72%, outperforming other methods. This work introduces a novel hybrid approach for EEG-based stroke severity classification, demonstrating that generative augmentation, when integrated properly, can significantly improve performance on small clinical datasets. To the best of our knowledge, this combination of techniques has not been explored before on any dataset, providing a solid foundation for future research in automated EEG-based stroke diagnosis.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Neuroradiology, Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Corporate Member of Freie Universität Berlin and Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Berlin, Ger
after.abstract: Background: Accessing routinely collected clinical data for research remains technically demanding across heterogeneous hospital systems. This proof-of-concept study aimed to evaluate the accuracy and query-level traceability of a commercial natural-language (NL) data-query platform implemented at a university hospital. Methods: An on-premises data integration platform with an NL query interface (AIRE; Briya, Tel Aviv, Israel) was connected to the institutional health data platform across three tertiary-care hospitals under an approved pseudonymization and governance framework. Implementation comprised regulatory and governance approval, and IT deployment. Twenty-five NL prompts addressing cohort identification and characterization in an adult ICD-10 C71-coded brain-tumor cohort (n = 1,594) were evaluated against manually written reference SQL and checked for a corresponding executed query in the exported log. Responses were classified into five categories. Prompts with unanswered or incorrect responses were re-posed in a new thread. Results: The platform was implemented over two years. Fifteen of 25 responses were exact (n = 11), concordant after definition alignment (n = 1), or incorrect but traceable from the logged SQL (n = 3); six were plausible but incorrect without a logged query, and four remained unanswered. No incorrect unlogged result recurred in a new thread. Across the initial and repeat evaluations, 22 of 23 logged responses were correct or traceable, whereas all eight unlogged responses were incorrect. Conclusions: Implementation was feasible but required substantial local institutional preparation. The NL interface reproduced SQL-derived results when definitions were explicit, while query-level provenance and verification of the displayed result were critical for identifying unreliable outputs.

after.title: Preprint: Awareness, support, and motivation surrounding the Canadian Dental Care Plan
after.authors: Pessoa, G. C.; Baltus, T. H. L.; Youssef, C.; Reimer, E.; Menon, A.; Lockman, N.; Schroth, R. J.
after.abstract: Objective: The Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) was introduced to provide dental insurance for low-income residents of Canada. The purpose of this study was to investigate CDCP awareness, support, alongside motivators to apply for the plan among a national sample of Canadian residents. Methods: Data from a national cross-sectional public opinion survey conducted before CDCP implementation, on behalf of Health Canada's Oral Health Branch, were analyzed. The survey included 2,250 participants from urban and rural/remote communities across Canada and assessed baseline awareness of the CDCP and barriers to dental care. Data were obtained from the Government of Canada Publications online archive. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were applied to evaluate associations among CDCP awareness, support, and motivators, with sociodemographic covariates. Statistical significance was set at p [≤] 0.05. Results: Overall, 42.7% of respondents had heard of the CDCP, with lower awareness among females, younger adults, those with lower education, those employed, and those never married. Female parents and younger adults were more likely to have searched for CDCP information, most commonly through news and media (53.0%). Overall, 81.5% supported the CDCP, with greater support among those without dental insurance, with university education, and those from Atlantic Canada, British Columbia, Yukon, Northwest Territories, and Nunavut. Meanwhile, opposition was higher in the Prairie Provinces. Leading motivators for applying included the extent of coverage offered, prospect of a better dental health, and whether the enrollment process would be easy. Uninsured participants were significantly more likely to apply for the CDCP if they reported having a good understanding of the plan, lived close to an oral health professional, and had urgent dental needs. Conclusion: Despite low pre-implementation awareness, pre-implementation support for the CDCP was high. Results can serve as a national baseline of CDCP awareness and support to measure changes in the public's views of the CDCP, and its potential role in improving access to essential oral health care in Canada. Based on these observations, follow-up studies are essential to evaluate the program's reach, development and uptake following implementation.

after.authors: Figueiredo, J. A.; Alves, H.; Moreira, C.; Ribeiro, A. I.
after.author_corresponding_institution: CEGOT - Centre of Studies in Geography and Spatial Planning, Faculty of Arts and Humanities of Porto, University of Porto, Via Panorâmica s/n, 4150-564 Porto, P
after.abstract: Gentrification is a global, accelerating urban process involving complex socio-spatial transformations. Although increasingly recognised as a determinant of urban health, quantitative evidence on its population health impacts remains scarce and inconsistent, limiting evidence-informed urban policymaking, especially in rapidly gentrifying contexts. Thus, we assessed the health impact of neighbourhood-level gentrification among adults in Porto (Northern Portugal), a hotspot of transnational gentrification. A quasi-experimental study was conducted using data from the EPIPorto population-based cohort (1999-2022), with 2,485 participants at baseline. A validated, context-sensitive 16-variable index of transnational gentrification, derived from 2011 and 2021 census and tourism-accommodation data through Principal Component Analysis, enabled neighbourhood classification as gentrifying or non-gentrifying. Difference-in-differences models estimated the effect of living in gentrifying neighbourhoods on ten cardiometabolic and behavioural outcomes. Inverse probability of censoring weighting was used to account for loss to follow-up and missing data. At baseline, 26.2% of participants resided in gentrifying neighbourhoods. Residence in a gentrifying neighbourhood was associated with a statistically significant reduction in nightly sleep duration (-0.346 h; 95% CI -0.650, -0.042), with statistically significant reductions in the lower-education and [≥]65-year subgroups. No significant effects were observed for body mass index, overweight/obesity, total/HDL/LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, and tobacco or alcohol use. Transnational gentrification in Porto showed limited effects on most cardiometabolic outcomes but was associated with reduced sleep duration, suggesting that the health impacts of gentrification may initially emerge through psychosocial pathways before translating into measurable cardiometabolic changes.

No significant effects were observed for body mass index, overweight/obesity, total/HDL/LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, and tobacco or alcohol use. after.title: Preprint: Mapping inequalities in dementia diagnosis in England: a Bayesian spatial analysis of disease prevalence and case ascertainment
after.authors: Taylor, B.; Jiang, J.; Warren, J. D.; Crutch, S. J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: The Bartlett Centre for Advanced Spatial Analysis, University College London, London, UK
after.abstract: Background: By 2030, over one million people in the UK are projected to be living with dementia; however, the NHS estimates that only approximately 65\% of individuals with dementia currently receive a formal diagnosis. Understanding the geographic and socioeconomic factors contributing to variation in diagnosis is essential for reducing inequalities in dementia care. Methods: We developed a Bayesian spatial modelling framework to separate underlying dementia prevalence from case ascertainment using routinely collected public datasets at Local Authority District (LAD) level across England. Underlying prevalence was modelled using non-modifiable and modifiable risk factors identified by the Lancet Commission, while diagnosis rates were modelled as a function of healthcare provision and sociodemographic factors. Spatial random effects were incorporated to identify residual geographic variation after accounting for observed covariates. We additionally compared case ascertainment with regional variation in dementia subtype coding as a further measure of diagnostic quality. Findings: Substantial geographic variation in dementia diagnosis remained after accounting for differences in underlying disease prevalence. Urbanicity, deprivation, ethnicity, and healthcare provision were associated with variation in case ascertainment, with spatial effects explaining additional regional variation. Diagnostic specificity varied considerably between regions, with areas of lower case ascertainment tending to exhibit higher proportions of undifferentiated dementia diagnoses. Interpretation: By jointly modelling underlying dementia prevalence and case ascertainment, we can distinguish the factors associated with dementia burden from those associated with diagnosis. This enables the identification of areas with low case ascertainment, which when combined with poor diagnostic specificity, provides an evidence base for targeted regional interventions. Potential interventions include strengthening dementia care pathways through enhanced outreach, more equitable access to diagnostic assessment, and locally tailored models of care.

after.title: Preprint: Exploring the Barriers and Facilitators of Vaccine Procurement in Health Districts of the South West Region of Cameroon
after.authors: Theophile, F. B.; Fru-Cho, J.; Fankam, N. F.; Tabi, E. S. B.; Yoah, T. A.; Akoachere, J.-F. T. K.
after.abstract: Background Immunization is the most cost-effective way of preventing vaccine-preventable diseases and reducing morbidity and mortality in children 0 to 5 years old. The vaccine procurement capacity of health districts significantly influences the vaccine coverage rates. The advent of the socio-political crisis in the North West and South West Regions of Cameroon could have had a negative bearing on vaccine procurement and thus coverage rates. Thus, this study was carried out to explore the barriers and facilitators of vaccine procurement in health districts of a South West Region of Cameroon. This will help reduce vaccine stock-out at the health district level and increase vaccine coverage. Methodology A qualitative study was conducted using in-depth interviews (IDIs) to collect data from healthcare providers in all the 21 health districts in the South West Region working with the Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI), and who met the inclusion criteria. A Delphi consensus approach was employed to formulate feasible facilitators to the optimization of vaccine procurement. Data was analysed using Nvivo 11. Thematic analysis was used to explore the barriers to vaccine procurement at the level of health districts. A Delphi consensus of [≥] 70.0% was considered acceptable. Results From the thematic analysis, nine broad themes: financial constraints, limited workforce, inadequate transportation logistics, poor equipment, inadequate managerial skills, inadequate in-service training, vaccine stock-out and weak primary health care (PHC) system facilities emerged as barriers to vaccine procurement . Of the 12 strategies retained for the optimization of vaccine procurement, 5 (41.7%) were priority strategies: provision of extra solar refrigerators (100.0%), WHO certification training for EPI staff (100.0%), financial allocation for transport (100.0%), equipment and training, in-service training for both district and health facility staff (100.0%), resolving the socio-political crisis (100.0%) and provision of specialized transport logistics for maritime Health Districts (100.0%). Conclusion Financing of vaccine procurement, recruitment/certification of staff, provision of transportation logistics, provision of solar refrigerators, regular supervision, organization of in-service training, with focus on requisition/stock and bulk-requisition were the main strategies suggested to overcome the barriers to vaccine procurement. Recommendations These findings highlight the need for all stakeholders to co-finance and manage vaccine procurement at the health district level in the South West Region of Cameroon.

after.title: Preprint: The Antipsychotic Load (AP_Load2026): a normalised prescribed-dose index for schizophrenia research
after.authors: Fernandez-Egea, E.; Krishnadas, R.; Jenkins, C.; Patel, R.; Cardinal, R. N.; Wolpe, N.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Psychiatry, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK; Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust (CPFT), Cambridge, UK
after.abstract: Background and Hypothesis Schizophrenia research routinely reduces antipsychotic treatment to a single number, but the available summaries disagree. Chlorpromazine equivalents, the WHO Defined Daily Dose (DDD) and the percentage of the licensed maximum (%BNFmax) rank the same patient differently, most of all for clozapine, whose dose-concentration relationship varies several-fold with sex and smoking. We hypothesised that referencing clozapine dose to a target individualised for sex and smoking would track plasma clozapine better than dose-proportional measures. Study Design In the Antipsychotic Load (AP_Load2026), each daily dose is expressed as a percentage of a reference dose, summed without a cap. Clozapine is referenced to a target individualised for sex and cigarettes per day, under two published anchor schemes, and other antipsychotics to a dose reconciling the WHO DDD and the licensed maximum. The clozapine term was tested against plasma clozapine (1316 assessments, 255 patients) with log-log mixed-effects models, and the non-clozapine reference against independently derived published doses. Study Results The individualised reference tracked plasma clozapine better than any dose-proportional measure (marginal R^2 0.249 vs. 0.166; deltaR^2 0.082, 95% CI 0.044-0.120). The scheme with the larger smoking correction fitted better (0.249 vs. 0.231), an ordering robust to quality-control variants and co-prescription. Of five candidate references for other antipsychotics, %BNFmax was the least consistent with external criteria. Conclusions AP_Load2026 is a transparent framework for normalising prescribed antipsychotic dose. Its clozapine reference is validated against a biomarker, whereas the reference for other antipsychotics is a calibrated convention at least comparable with existing alternatives. The index is particularly suited to treatment-resistant and clozapine-enriched cohorts.

data.summary: added: Preprint: Wealth inequalities malaria parasitaemia and child anaemia in Nigeria

after.title: Preprint: Wealth inequalities malaria parasitaemia and child anaemia in Nigeria
after.authors: Fowobaje, K. R.; Adegbenro, A.; Lawson, T.
after.abstract: Anaemia and malaria remain concentrated among children living in poorer households in Nigeria, but the extent to which the wealth gradient in anaemia operates through current malaria parasitaemia is uncertain. We used three nationally representative surveys to estimate a clearly defined parasitaemia-mediated component of the association, while recognising that anaemia has multiple infectious, nutritional, genetic, and social causes. We analysed de facto children aged 6-59 months in the 2010, 2015, and 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Surveys. Within each survey, we contrasted children in the poorest quintile with children in the richer and richest quintiles. The outcome was altitude-adjusted anaemia and the mediator was microscopy-confirmed parasitaemia. Weighted outcome and mediator models adjusted for child age and sex, maternal education, urban residence, geopolitical zone, household size, rainy-season interview, and altitude. We standardized interventional total, direct, and indirect effects using g-computation. Missing data were addressed with 20 chained-equation imputations; uncertainty used 1,000 Rao-Wu survey-bootstrap replicates. Analytic samples included 3,307, 3,643, and 6,572 children in 2010, 2015, and 2021. The multiple-imputation total risk difference was 11.0 (95% CI 4.1 to 17.9) percentage points in 2015 and 12.5 (95% CI 8.4 to 16.6) points in 2021; corresponding parasitaemia-mediated indirect differences were 3.4 (95% CI 1.4 to 5.4) and 2.0 (95% CI 1.1 to 2.9) points. The 2010 total-effect interval included zero. Proportion-mediated estimates were withheld for 2010 and 2015 because of unstable total-effect denominators. The poorest-to-richer/richest contrast was associated with higher anaemia risk in 2015 and 2021. A smaller positive component was compatible with mediation through microscopy-confirmed parasitaemia. Because wealth, parasitaemia, and haemoglobin were measured in the same survey visit, the estimates require assumptions about temporal ordering and unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding; they do not establish that eliminating parasitaemia would remove the observed anaemia inequality.

after.title: Preprint: Implementing community-based minimally invasive tissue sampling for mortality surveillance in rural South Africa: A process evaluation of the Vukamberi project
after.authors: Mondlane, Z. L.; Kahn, K.; Chipungu, S.; Wagner, R. G.; Tippett Barr, B.; Price, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of the Witwatersrand Faculty of Health Sciences
after.abstract: Accurate cause-of-death data are limited in rural low- and middle-income settings, where most deaths occur at home without medical certification. Minimally invasive tissue sampling (MITS) is a culturally acceptable alternative to complete autopsy but has largely been applied to stillbirths and child deaths. We evaluated the process and implementation of a community-based, all-age MITS study in rural South Africa. The Vukamberi project ("to examine" in Xitsonga) is a prospective study in rural Bushbuckridge sub-district, Mpumalanga Province. Guided by the Medical Research Council Framework for Complex Interventions and Proctors Implementation Outcomes Framework, we assessed reach, adoption, fidelity, feasibility, acceptability and timeliness using prospectively collected records of deaths notified between 07 July 2024 to 30 June 2026, and mapped challenges to adaptive strategies by domain and phase. All 408 notified community deaths were screened, and 316 (77.5%) were eligible. Families consented for 206 eligible cases (65.2%), all of which proceeded to MITS, with target-organ sampling adherence in 199 (96.6%). Median time from death to notification was 15 hours (interquartile range [IQR] 5-23) and to MITS completion 37 hours (IQR 25-49). Enrolled decedents were 197 adults (95.6%) and 9 paediatric cases (4.4%). Main ineligibility reasons were in-hospital death (excluded by design; 27 cases) and notification beyond 48 hours (26 cases). Family refusal, mostly reflecting grief-related unreadiness and sociocultural barriers, accounted for 53 (48.2%) non-enrolled eligible cases. Adaptive strategies that increased enrolment included extending recruitment beyond the Agincourt Health and Socio-Demographic Surveillance System into the wider sub-district, incentivised community informants, elder-mediated consent, gender-appropriate field staff, non-disfigurement messaging in local languages and mortuary-based consenting where household access was restricted by a traditional leader. Community-based MITS was feasible in this rural setting. Culturally responsive consent strategies, mortuary partnerships and multi-channel death notification helped overcome sociocultural and logistical barriers, and a reliable supply of consumables proved essential for continuous enrolment. These findings may inform community-based mortality surveillance in other low- and middle-income settings.

after.title: Preprint: MLX-Radiomics: accelerating standardized regional and voxel-wise radiomics for CT, PET and MRI
after.authors: Sandoval, J.; Sandoval, A.; Saleem, A.
after.abstract: Background: Differences among radiomics implementations complicate cross-study comparisons, while voxel-wise feature extraction remains computationally demanding. We developed MLX-Radiomics to accelerate regional feature extraction and voxel-wise mapping while preserving agreement with standardized reference measurements. Methods: MLX-Radiomics implements 172 feature definitions from the Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI), 16 extensions and the IBSI 2 image filters. We assessed agreement with IBSI reference data and evaluated numerical accuracy against independent double-precision and analytic calculations. In matched comparisons on Apple M1 Max and M5 Max systems, we used the IBSI reference CT to compare feature values, extraction time and memory use with PyRadiomics, MIRP and Flash-Radiomics, and feature values with FastRad. Separately, we compared the time required to generate voxel-wise feature maps for regions of up to 10.1 million voxels with published GPU results obtained on different hardware and images. We evaluated agreement with MIRP under published settings in a 51-patient cohort with CT, FDG PET and T1-weighted MRI. Results: MLX-Radiomics agreed with all 2,160 IBSI reference measurements within the specified tolerances. With matching outputs, MLX-Radiomics was 2.66 to 7.27 times faster than PyRadiomics and MIRP for regional feature extraction and 198 to 218 times faster than PyRadiomics for voxel-wise mapping on a 24 x 24 x 24-voxel crop. It also outperformed the fastest Flash-Radiomics CPU configurations tested. On the M5 Max, generating 93 maps over 10.1 million voxels took 23.8 s. In the patient cohort, MLX-Radiomics and MIRP agreed on 98.0% of requested values. For tumors at the image edge, matching the libraries' resampling rules substantially improved agreement. Conclusions: MLX-Radiomics provides standardized regional measurements and voxel-wise maps for CT, PET and MRI, with evidence of faster extraction limited to CT. It can support quantitative imaging research on relatively inexpensive hardware without requiring a separate GPU workstation.

after.authors: chen, y.; Zhang, J.; Wang, S.; Zhou, Q.; Li, X.; Li, J.; Luo, T.; Feng, C.; Hu, Z.; Luo, J.; Liao, X.; Fan, G.; Pang, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Spine Surgery, The Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, No. 600 Tianhe Road, Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510630, Guangdong Province
after.abstract: Spine Endoscopic Atlas-Tissue (SEA-T) is a multicenter dataset for pixel-level multi-class semantic segmentation in endoscopic spine surgery. It contains 3,310 expert-annotated frames from 65 patients (1,663 cervical frames from 39 patients; 1,647 lumbar frames from 26 patients) across three centers, plus 11,155 unlabeled frames. after.title: Preprint: The effects of exercise and physical activity on gait biomechanics and pain in knee osteoarthritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
after.authors: Bytheway, N.; Amor, S.; Swinton, P.; Cheah, K.; Morrison, A.; Samvelyan, H. J.
after.abstract: Objectives To evaluate the effects of exercise and physical activity on gait biomechanics and pain in adults with knee osteoarthritis. Methods Systematic searches were performed of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and SPORTDiscus databases for controlled intervention studies published up to 31 December 2024. Eligible studies included adults with knee osteoarthritis undertaking exercise or physical activity compared with control group(s). Risk of bias was assessed using the Downs and Black Checklist. Bayesian three-level hierarchical random-effects meta-analyses synthesised standardised mean differences (SMD; effect size) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Results Of 2,602 records identified, 18 studies involving 1,102 participants (345 males and 757 females) were included. Exercise and physical activity reduced pain (SMD 0.61, 95% CrI 0.29 to 0.92) and improved spatiotemporal gait parameters (SMD 0.67, 95% CrI 0.27 to 1.05). Improvements were reported across several intervention types, including strengthening, aerobic, multicomponent, and mind-body exercise. Effects on knee kinematics (SMD 0.12, 95% CrI -0.18 to 0.41) and kinetics (SMD -0.03, 95% CrI -0.25 to 0.18) were small or uncertain. Conclusions Exercise and physical activity may improve pain and spatiotemporal gait characteristics in knee osteoarthritis, but consistent improvements in knee kinematics and kinetics were not demonstrated. Further adequately powered trials with standardised biomechanical assessments and longer assessments are needed.

after.title: Preprint: User-Informed Design of a Psychological Support Social Pet Robot for Community-Dwelling People With Long-Term Physical Disabilities: A Formative Study
after.authors: Lu, Y.; Chen, X.; Hui, R.; Dai, Y.; Mei, X.; So, H.; Li, C.; Tao, X.; Li, Y.
after.author_corresponding_institution: School of Nursing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
after.abstract: Background. Community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities may experience pain that interferes with daily and social activities and is associated with poorer mental wellbeing. A home-based psychological support social pet robot could offer mood check-ins, companionship, supportive interaction, and mindfulness guidance for community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities. Preliminary evidence is needed to understand their preferences and translate them into candidate design requirements. Objective. This study aimed to identify preliminary needs and preferences to inform a psychological support social pet robot for community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities, offering mood check-ins, companionship, and mindfulness guidance at home. Methods. We conducted a 3-phase formative user-informed design study comprising initial concept development, qualitative target user interviews, and a design workshop. Six community-dwelling adults with long-term physical disabilities took part in the interviews, and one participant also answered the workshop questions by telephone. Four authors used modified workshop materials to synthesize the interview findings and separate responses into an early product plan. Results. Qualitative content analysis of the interview transcripts produced 5 themes. These were emotional support, soft touch and appearance, mindfulness delivery, context of use, and ease of use and accessibility. Participants expressed preferences about companionship, touch, use settings, and interaction effort. The author workshop combined these findings with author and technical judgments to develop candidate requirements for dialogue and mindfulness delivery. The resulting psychological support concept combined mood check-ins and companion-oriented interaction with flexible mindfulness guidance. The design also needed to consider pain and daily routines. After the workshop, the authors developed a physical proof-of-concept prototype. It implemented only part of the candidate requirements and included additional author or technical choices. Conclusions. For this small community-dwelling sample, target user input showed that home use, physical access, companionship, and flexible support were important. Mindfulness was one component of the broader psychological support role, alongside mood check-ins and optional companion interaction. The prototype illustrates but does not validate the early requirements. Further studies should include people with a wider range of long-term physical disabilities and test usability, accessibility, privacy, and nursing value. Keywords. social pet robots; user-informed design; psychological support; mindfulness; long-term physical disabilities; community dwelling; user centered design; human robot interaction; mental health; qualitative research
