after.title: Preprint: Sex- and Age-Specific Associations of Blood Lead Levels with Child Growth and Haemoglobin in Bangladesh: A Nationally Representative Study
after.authors: Patwary, M. M.; Ashraf, S.; Islam, M. A.; Browning, M. H. E. M.; Bell, M. L.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Environment and Sustainability Research Initiative, Khulna, Bangladesh
after.abstract: Evidence on sex- and age-specific associations between lead levels and childhood growth remains limited. We analyzed 10,324 children aged 12-59 months from the Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2025 using survey-weighted multivariable linear regression to examine sex- and age-specific associations of blood lead level (BLL) with anthropometric measures and haemoglobin levels. The geometric mean BLL was 4.43 {micro}g/dL, and 66.3% of children had concentrations above the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) threshold ([≥]3.5 {micro}g/dL). Higher BLL was associated with lower height-for-age z-score (HAZ) ({beta} = -0.129, 95% CI: -0.182 to -0.076), weight-for-age z-score (WAZ) ({beta} = -0.108, 95% CI: -0.156 to -0.060), and weight-for-height z-score (WHZ) ({beta} = -0.052, 95% CI: -0.101 to -0.002). Higher BLL was also associated with lower HAZ and WAZ among boys (HAZ: {beta} = -0.114, 95% CI: -0.188 to -0.040; WAZ: {beta} = -0.113, 95% CI: -0.179 to -0.046) and girls (HAZ: {beta} = -0.150, 95% CI: -0.225 to -0.075; WAZ: {beta} = -0.104, 95% CI: -0.171 to -0.036), while higher BLL was associated with lower WHZ among boys ({beta} = -0.076, 95% CI: -0.144 to -0.007). Higher BLL was associated with lower HAZ ({beta} = -0.266, 95% CI: -0.408 to -0.125) and WAZ ({beta} = -0.206, 95% CI: -0.326 to -0.086) among boys aged 24-35 months, while among girls aged 36-59 months, corresponding estimates were -0.211 (95% CI: -0.310 to -0.113) and -0.106 (95% CI: -0.191 to -0.022). The findings suggest that longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal and developmental patterns underlying these associations.

after.title: Preprint: Development and pilot evaluation of ACE-T, a nurse-focused delirium initial-response tool, across three health systems
after.authors: Cours, A.; Trabert, J.; Higgins, M.; Saleem, U.; Sampson, E.; Storr-Street, N.; MacLullich, A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Section of Geriatric Medicine, Primary Care and Population Health, Department of Medicine, Stanford University School of Medicine, Palo Alto, CA, USA
after.abstract: Background A positive delirium screen should trigger timely assessment and care, but the initial bedside response is not always clearly defined. ACE-T (Acute Triggers / Patient Experience / Treatments) is a nurse-led tool (www.theace-t.com) that sets out initial care actions and supports documentation and team communication. Objectives To assess perceived usability and utility, refine the tool, and describe documentation before and after its introduction at three hospitals. Methods In this developmental pilot, 53 multidisciplinary staff completed a structured survey and provided free-text feedback. We also reviewed a non-random sample of 60 records: 10 before and 10 after ACE-T introduction at each site. Prespecified delirium-care actions documented within 48 hours of the first positive delirium screen or documented diagnosis were summarised descriptively by site. Results ACE-T was rated easy or very easy to use by 75% (39/52), clear or very clear by 77% (41/53), and very or extremely helpful for improving delirium care by 71% (37/52). Feedback guided revisions to clarify professional roles, fit clinical workflows and strengthen person-centred prompts. Documentation of delirium or suspected delirium was more frequent after introduction at all three sites: 1/10 before versus 10/10 after in Germany, 0/10 versus 10/10 in the UK, and 3/10 versus 9/10 in the USA. Changes in documentation of other assessments varied by site. Conclusion ACE-T is a promising nurse-led tool for initial delirium care. Positive staff ratings and more frequent delirium documentation support its further development and prospective evaluation. It offers nurses a practical starting point for what to do next when delirium is detected.

after.authors: Chick, G.; Gbesemete, D. F.; Jump Salcedo, P.; Wilson, M. W.; Hill, A. R.; Coutinho, T. J.; Anderson, R.; Elliott, R. S.; Mohanraj, D.; Cleary, D. W.; Lucidarme, J.; Borrow, R.; Faust, S. N.; Gorringe, A. R.; Read, R. C.; Dale, A. P.; Laver, J. R.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Controlled Human Infection Group, School of Clinical & Experimental Sciences, Faculty of Medicine, University of Southampton, Southampton, UK
after.abstract: Introduction Previous work has shown that experimentally induced colonisation with Neisseria lactamica (Nlac) is safe and associated with reduced meningococcal colonisation. This pilot study aims to establish the safety, induction of colonisation and immunogenicity following intranasal inoculation with a mixture of four strains of genetically modified Nlac (GM-Nlac). Each of these strains express meningococcal vaccine antigens present in current vaccines: Neisseria adhesin A (NadA) and one of four different variants of Factor H-binding protein (FHbp), the latter of which is specifically mutated to abrogate its ability to bind the human complement protein, Factor H. Methods and analysis In this controlled human infection model experiment, 10 healthy participants aged 18-45 years will be inoculated with a mixture of 4 strains of GM-Nlac (collectively referred to as the challenge agent, 4xrNlac). They will be followed up over 28 days to assess colonisation, immunogenicity and efficacy of eradication with a single oral dose of ciprofloxacin (500 mg). Participant contacts will also be recruited to assess for onward transmission of GM-Nlac. Ethics and dissemination This study involves the deliberate release of four genetically modified organisms, which has been approved by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (reference: 25/R50/01). The clinical study has also been approved by South-Central Oxford A Research Ethics Committee and the Health Research Authority (reference: 26/SC/0072). All participants will provide written informed consent prior to enrolment. Findings of the study will be submitted for publication in a peer-reviewed scientific journal and for presentation at scientific conferences. Registration This study is registered on the ISRCTN registry with study registration number ISRCTN10930766

after.title: Preprint: Implementing a Group Education Model for People with Type 2 Diabetes in a Socioeconomically Deprived Primary Care Population: A Quality Improvement Report
after.authors: Bond, E.; Sennett, J.; Veighey, K.
after.abstract: People with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) receiving injectable therapies require ongoing education and support to optimise self-management and glycaemic control. Group education may offer a cost-effective approach that combines professional guidance with peer support. Homewell Practice serves a socioeconomically deprived population in Hampshire with significant health inequalities. Many patients receiving insulin or GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy had poor glycaemic control, frailty, or increased risk of hospital admission. Traditional one-to-one consultations provided limited opportunities for peer learning and support. A 12-month quality improvement project was conducted between May 2022 and April 2023. Adults with T2DM receiving injectable therapy were invited to attend monthly community-based education sessions. Attendance data, HbA1c outcomes and patient feedback were collected and analysed descriptively. Patient-centred group sessions were delivered using adult-learning principles and peer discussion. Topics included insulin titration, hypoglycaemia management, nutrition, glycaemic targets and diabetes complications. Fifteen patients attended at least one session. Improvements in glycaemic control were associated with repeated attendance. Mean HbA1c reduction was 12.4% in patients attending four or more sessions, compared with 5.6% for those attending three sessions and 2.4% for those attending two sessions. Patients attending only one session demonstrated a 1.8% increase in HbA1c. All questionnaire respondents (9/9, 100%) reported improved understanding of diabetes and found the sessions useful; 8/9 would recommend the programme. Peer support was identified as the most valued aspect of participation. Attendance remained lower than anticipated, particularly among patients with multiple comorbidities and mental health needs. Group education for adults receiving injectable diabetes therapy was associated with high patient satisfaction and improved glycaemic outcomes among regular attendees. A hybrid model combining group education with individualised support may improve accessibility and engagement for higher-need patients.

We assessed discrimination and calibration at 10 years overall, by age and ethnicity. We compared characteristics of patients with a 10-year QRISK4-Lifetime risk [≥] 10% with an equal-sized group selected using lifetime risk to age 95 Results There were 202,424 CVD events in the English derivation cohort of 9,976,306 people and 65,253 events in the validation cohort of 3,246,602 people. after.abstract: CRISPR-based detection technologies have the potential to enable precise, rapid, and cost-effective diagnostic and biosurveillance solutions by pairing sensitive and specific nucleic acid detection with a simple workflow. Combining isothermal amplification and CRISPR detection in a single reaction as a "one-pot" detection method can meet these needs, but only if the CRISPR enzyme remains active at the temperatures and salt concentrations that isothermal amplification requires. Here we describe MB-CasFire, a CRISPR-Cas enzyme engineered from a naturally thermostable Cas12a for improved stability and performance, as a "plug-and-play" DETECTR(R) (DNA Endonuclease-Targeted CRISPR Trans Reporter) enzyme for sensitive and specific nucleic acid detection. MB-CasFire remains active at elevated temperatures in amplification buffers and supports one-pot detection with loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and nicking enzyme amplification reaction (NEAR), eliminating transfers between amplification and readout, and increasing the signal-to-noise to enable precise nucleic acid detection. This method, called OnePot DETECTR, is also compatible with commercially available isothermal master mixes, including those from New England Biolabs, allowing assays to be assembled from standard reagents. Using MB-CasFire, we detected SARS-CoV-2 in nasal swab samples with a LAMP-based OnePot DETECTR assay and Neisseria gonorrhoeae in urine samples with a NEAR-based OnePot DETECTR assay. MB-CasFire also functioned in multiplex detection and single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination assays for antibiotic resistance genotyping. These results support MB-CasFire as a versatile detection enzyme that simplifies assay architecture for CRISPR-based detection assays that amplify, recognize, and report the presence of nucleic acid targets in a single reaction without thermocycling.

after.abstract: Background: Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are incompletely utilized in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). The degree to which use varies at the individual level and within specialties is unknown. We aimed to characterize provider-level and specialty-level variation in ARNI and SGLT2i prescribing after HF hospitalization. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included Veterans Affairs (VA) providers seeing patients within 6 months of HFrEF hospitalization 2017-2023. We used descriptive statistics and site-adjusted multilevel logistic regression to examine prescribing by medical specialty, provider type, and provider sex. Adjusted median odds ratios (mOR) and empirical (unadjusted) provider-level rate ratios (RRs) by percentile were used to describe provider-level variation. Clinical pharmacy visits were assessed as an independent factor and as an interaction with specialty. Results: Among 7,946 providers caring for 76,795 patients across 211,267 outpatient encounters, provider-level variation remained substantial after adjustment for patient characteristics and site-level clustering (mOR 1.45 for ARNI; 1.46 for SGLT2i). Within every specialty, providers ranged from near-zero to near-100% use. Relative to the median provider in the same specialty, RRs ranged from 0-0.31 (5th percentile), 0.37-0.71 (25th), 1.38-1.66 (75th), to 1.8-3.2 (95th). Cardiology visits carried the highest adjusted odds of ARNI (OR 2.30, 95% CI 2.18-2.44) and SGLT2i use (OR 1.99, 95% CI 1.88-2.11) and most new starts. Pharmacist visits were independently associated with greater use of ARNI (OR 1.14, 1.06-1.23) and SGLT2i (OR 1.15, 1.06-1.24), with no effect modification by specialty. In early 2023, 58.4% (ARNI) and 40.2% (SGLT2i) of post-hospitalization HF visits had untreated patients. Conclusions: Provider-level variation in ARNI and SGLT2i use after guideline incorporation was large within every specialty and independent of site effects. Though specific specialties have higher use, individual providers, not specialty alone, may be an important target for efforts to close gaps in therapy.

after.authors: Cheuyem, F. Z. L.; Tchamani, R.; Touko, A. D.; Achangwa, C.; Mapouo, C. J. K.; Fouodjeu, G. C. M.; Nouko, A.; Modibo, S.

after.abstract: Background: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and tuberculosis (TB) form one of the deadliest syndemics, and sub-Saharan Africa bears over 80% of HIV-associated TB deaths. In Cameroon, evidence on HIV/TB coinfection remains unsynthesized across regions and populations, obscuring the national burden. Hence, we estimated the prevalence of HIV/TB coinfection and treatment outcomes in Cameroon. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO: CRD420261399169), we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, African Journals Online, and grey literature for English- and French-language studies conducted in Cameroon. Reports were independently screened, their data extracted, and their methodology appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Random-effects models pooled prevalence, treatment outcomes, and adjusted odds ratios. Heterogeneity was assessed with I2. Results: Seventy studies (1995-2023) were included, 87.1% at low risk of bias. Pooled HIV prevalence among TB patients was 29.2% (95% CI: 26.3-32.3; 67 studies; n=57,169; I2 = 97.8%), with no significant evidence of publication bias. Prevalence was higher from 2007 onwards (29.9%; 62 studies; n=55,358) than before (20.5%; 5 studies; n=1,811). It was highest in the North-West (41.9%; 7 studies; n=6,324) versus Littoral (25.0%; 15 studies; n=10,419) and West (23.8%; 6 studies; n=4,206); and in extrapulmonary TB (42.3%; 3 studies; n=371) versus mixed forms (37.7%; 21 studies; n=37,239) and pulmonary TB (23.9%; 37 studies; n=16,096) (all p<0.05). Among coinfected patients, pooled treatment success was 75.9% (95% CI: 70.4-80.8; 8 studies; n=4,230), mortality 21.1% (95% CI: 11.9-34.7; 10 studies; n=4,403), loss to follow-up 7.7% (95% CI: 4.3-13.3; 5 studies; n=3,103), and treatment failure 0.3% (95% CI: 0.1-1.5; 6 studies; n=3,520). Lack of antiretroviral therapy (ART) increased the odds of unfavorable outcomes (AOR = 1.90; 95% CI: 1.15-3.12; 2 studies). Conclusions: Approximately three in ten TB patients in Cameroon are coinfected with HIV, with marked regional and clinical variation. Treatment success remains below national targets. Strengthening TB-HIV service integration, routine HIV testing, and timely ART initiation and continuation is essential to reduce the HIV-associated TB morbidity and mortality in the country.

after.title: Preprint: Molecular evolution of Andes virus lineages leading to recent human outbreaks
after.authors: Sharma, C.; Oversti, S.; Stass, R.; Lucaci, A. G.; Audet, J.; Safronetz, D.; Zhao, L.; Lythgoe, K.; Katzourakis, A.; Bowden, T. A.; Lytras, S.; Ghafari, M.
after.abstract: Andes virus (ANDV) is exceptional among hantaviruses in its capacity for person-to-person transmission, but whether outbreaks reflect recent viral adaptation or emergence of pre-existing reservoir lineages remains unclear. We generated paired blood- and nasal-derived genomes from the MV Hondius outbreak and integrated them with a segment-linked collection of human- and rodent-derived ANDV sequences, including incomplete genomes. We developed a linkage-informed missing-segment framework that preserves isolate identity, sampling time, and cross-segment placement without imputing nucleotide states, enabling sensitivity analyses of patchy segment coverage. Across five human outbreaks, dated phylogenies placed outbreak lineages independently within geographically structured reservoir diversity, with closest sampled ancestry predating detection. Time-dependent-rate analyses indicated a deeper reservoir-associated history, while mutation reconstruction, selection tests, branch-rate comparisons, and structural mapping found no recurrent adaptive transition preceding human transmission. MV Hondius samples showed minimal consensus-level diversification. These results shift attention from repeated recent adaptation toward deeper lineage properties and ecological opportunity.

after.authors: Villasenor, I.; Biswas, R.; Okpara, K.; Shirali, S.; Hu, J.-R.; Nicholas, S. B.; Tuot, D. S.; Errett, N. A.; Lamprea-Montealegre, J. A.
after.abstract: Background: Albuminuria testing to diagnose chronic kidney disease (CKD) and guide blood pressure management is recommended for adults with hypertension but remains underused in part due to suboptimal patient understanding of its importance. Patient facing behavioral interventions have the potential to bridge this gap. We developed and evaluated KnowCKD, a behaviorally informed intervention designed to increase patient awareness of CKD and knowledge and promote albuminuria testing among adults with hypertension. Methods: KnowCKD consisted of an educational infographic and brief, behaviorally informed messages delivered to patients' smartphones during the 5 days leading up to and including a scheduled primary care visit at one academic medical center. Among 57 adults with hypertension without diabetes or recent albuminuria testing, we assessed changes in CKD awareness and knowledge and patient-reported engagement via survey pre- and post- exposure to KnowCKD. Electronic Health Record (EHR)- confirmed albuminuria or proteinuria testing was compared with 182 contemporaneous primary care controls using unmatched and propensity score-matched analysis. A postintervention focus group evaluated participant experiences. Results: After exposure to KnowCKD, recognition that adults with hypertension should undergo urine testing increased from 58% to 95%, knowledge that albuminuria indicates protein in the urine increased from 47% to 95%, and awareness that testing facilitates early CKD detection increased from 55% to 100% (P <0.001 for all). After the primary care visit, 77% of patients reported asking their clinician about urine testing and 65% reported that testing was ordered. EHR-confirmed albuminuria or proteinuria testing occurred in 36.8% of KnowCKD participants versus 11.0% of controls (risk ratio, 3.35 [95% CI, 1.96-5.73]; absolute risk difference, 25.9 percentage points [95% CI, 12.5- 39.2]). The propensity score-matched risk ratio was 2.93 (95% CI, 1.59-5.42). Participants described KnowCKD as timely, understandable, and actionable and emphasized trusted health-system communication for broader implementation. Conclusions: KnowCKD was associated with increased patient awareness of CKD and knowledge, patient engagement, and higher EHR-confirmed albuminuria or proteinuria testing among adults with hypertension. A rigorous evaluation of KnowCKD implementation within routine health-system workflows is warranted as a next step.

after.abstract: Background: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is associated with poor outcomes. Risk factors for progressive CRS are not understood in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Objectives: This study aimed to determine the incidence of progressive CRS and risk factors in individuals with CKD. Methods: Adults with CKD in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study excluding those with heart failure (HF) at baseline were included (n = 3,557). We defined progressive CRS as developing HF and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) within 12 months. ESKD was defined as needing renal replacement therapy or renal transplant. The associations of baseline risk factors with progressive CRS were examined using Cox proportional hazards models. A sensitivity analysis assessed risk factors in those who developed HF before ESKD and vice versa. Results: 161 patients (4.5%) developed progressive CRS. after.abstract: Background: Capturing an electrocardiogram (ECG) during transient symptoms remains challenging in emergency department (ED) patients with palpitations. Following the IPED trial, a smartphone-based ambulatory ECG event recorder pathway was integrated into NHS care. We evaluated this service over five years, assessing diagnostic yield, management, one-year outcomes and predictors of cardiac arrhythmia. Methods: Single-centre service evaluation of consecutive patients referred with palpitations to a smartphone-based ambulatory ECG event recorder clinic between 24th July 2019 and 24th July 2024. Patients underwent event-triggered ECG monitoring using the single-lead Kardia Mobile (AliveCor, Inc.) or their own smartwatch with ECG capability. Clinical characteristics, rhythm recordings, investigations, one-year outcomes and management changes were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of one-year cardiac arrhythmia diagnosis. Results: 1750 patients attended the clinic, mean age 44.3 +/- 16.1 years, 58.2% female. 1176 patients (67.2%) underwent monitoring with a cardiac arrhythmia directly captured in 67 patients (5.7% of monitored), including atrial fibrillation (n=39), supraventricular tachycardia (13), atrial flutter (9), atrial tachycardia (5) and ventricular tachycardia (1). By one year, 84 (7.1%) who underwent monitoring received a cardiac diagnosis with 79.8% (67/84) established directly via clinic monitoring. Across the entire cohort (n=1750), 114 (6.5%) had a cardiac cause at one year, 1472 (84.2%) had non-cardiac aetiology and 1569 (89.1%) were discharged back to primary care. Medication changes were initiated in 106 patients (6.1%). Independent predictors of a one-year cardiac diagnosis were increasing age (aOR 1.04 per 1-year increase), prior atrial fibrillation/flutter (aOR 5.57) and a presenting symptom of irregular beating (aOR 2.65). Conclusion: Our service provides an effective model for evaluating ED patients with palpitations. Over five years the service reliably detected actionable cardiac arrhythmias while safely discharging nearly 90% of patients to primary care. Clinical characteristics may guide patient selection to maximise clinic efficiency.

after.abstract: The biological mechanisms governing recovery versus chronicity of adverse posttraumatic neuropsychiatric sequelae (APNS) remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized longitudinal molecular changes among trauma survivors across ten APNS domains, including pain, anxiety, and depression. Recovery across these diverse clinical outcomes was associated with a shared, temporally coordinated transcriptional signature, characterized by early innate immune activation, subsequent homeostatic and wound-healing processes, and later adaptive immune responses. In contrast, chronic APNS trajectories exhibited limited transcriptional remodeling. We derived and externally validated an RNA-based Recovery Score (RRS) capturing the shared molecular response underlying recovery. Higher RRS was associated with greater clinical recovery, elevated peritraumatic cortisol, and lower cumulative stress exposure. Drug-response profiling identified candidate compounds predicted to mimic recovery-associated transcriptional changes. Together, these findings support posttraumatic recovery as an active biological process and identify shared molecular pathways that may be harnessed to prevent multiple adverse posttraumatic outcomes.

after.authors: Ringleb, M.; Trampert, T.; Trampert, T.; Bloch, W.
after.abstract: Background: There is an increasing strain on our healthcare system due to rising numbers of diseases related to chronic stress. One approach to combat these stress-related complaints is health coaching. However, personal health coaching is expensive and time costly, while digital offers can complement the already existing health coaching strategies. Therefore, this study investigates the effects of an AI-supported, digital health and prevention program. Methods: 253 participants were included in the study, with 113 being analyzed eventually. General stress experience and self-efficacy were assessed at baseline (T1), after six weeks (T2), and three months after the interventional phase (T3) via a Numerical Analog Scale (NAS) with values ranging from 0 to 10, the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), and the PsyCap Scale (CPC). Results: A significant time effect was observed for CPC and PSS. CPC increased significantly from T1 to T2 and T3 and remained stable between T2 and T3, while PSS decreased from T1 to T2 and increased again by T3. All pairwise comparisons were significant. There were also significant time effects for self-reported current health status, health literacy, health awareness, and self-efficacy, with values at T3 being higher than at T1 (for health awareness, this was already evident at T2; for self-efficacy, this was additionally evident between T2 and T3), while no time effect was found for motivation. Conclusion: PREVERY seems to be an effective prevention program to increase psychological capital together with self-reported current health status, health awareness, health literacy, and self-efficacy, while at the same time reducing perceived stress.

after.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a highly heritable psychiatric disorder characterised by substantial clinical heterogeneity. While global polygenic scores (gPGS) capture genetic liability to SCZ, their ability to explain clinical variability remains limited. Pathway-stratified polygenic scores (sPGS) offer a biologically informed approach to patient stratification. In this study, common genetic variants were annotated across five neurotransmitter (NT) signalling pathways - acetylcholine (ACh), dopamine, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), glutamate (Glu), and serotonin. sPGS adjusted for sex and ancestry principal components, were calculated in two independent cohorts with different available clinical data (N=3,044 and N=645). By clustering top-decile individuals across the five sPGS dimensions, we classified patients into five mutually exclusive patient profiles, which were then evaluated for their associations with Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) symptom dimensions, age at disease onset (AAO), and three-year clinical remission and treatment response. Although gPGS showed no significant association with clinical outcomes, some sPGS-derived profiles captured clinically relevant heterogeneity across cohorts. Patients assigned to the Ach profile exhibited higher overall symptom severity, particularly negative symptoms and general psychopathology. Patients within the Glu profile were characterised by more severe negative symptoms, earlier AAO, reduced three-year remission, and poorer treatment response. Similarly, the GABA risk profile was also associated with three-year remission rates. These findings suggest that NT pathway-specific polygenic profiling may capture clinically relevant variation overlooked by genome-wide approaches. By identifying genetic profiles associated with symptom severity, disease onset, and longitudinal outcomes, this framework could contribute to biologically informed patient stratification and inform future precision psychiatry approaches in SCZ.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Institute for Global Health, University College London, UK
after.abstract: Background. Pupils enrolled in Alternative Provision (AP) represent a highly vulnerable population, with heightened mental health need at risk of long-term educational disengagement. Examining AP enrolment in relation to mental health-related school support and hospital contacts may inform early intervention and prevention approaches to address unmet mental health need. Methods. We analysed population-level linked school and hospital administrative data for 1.7m pupils (born 2000-2002) who attended state schools in England. We examined differences by racial-ethnic group and gender in rates and timing of AP enrolment and recording patterns of mental health-related provision and hospital contacts among pupils with AP enrolment. Results. A majority (62.4%) of pupils with AP enrolment had recorded mental health need, highest among Mixed White-Black Caribbean pupils (74.0%). Among those in AP, 52.0% of girls with a mental health-related hospital contact had school provision, compared to 67.3% boys. For some racial-ethnic groups, schools appeared less likely to record need evident in hospital records; 17.5% boys and 36.2% girls from Mixed White-Asian backgrounds enrolled in AP had mental health-related hospital contact without school provision. Conclusion. Among pupils enrolled in AP, documented mental health need is high but unevenly recorded across systems, with inequalities by racial-ethnic group and gender.

after.authors: Grandhe, K. K.; Riedel, T. E.
after.abstract: Loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) offers a promising alternative to PCR for low-resource settings, but practical barriers remain. For example there is often the need for reliable electricity, precision heating equipment, and cold-chain storage of reagents. Here, we describe a rudimentary but functional platform that integrates (i) a non-electric, chemically driven water bath capable of sustaining LAMP-relevant temperatures and (ii) lyophilized LAMP assays compatible with simple sample inputs such as diluted saliva or oral rinse. We demonstrate successful LAMP amplification under multiple heating configurations, including a thermos-based chemical bath and field-mimicking setups. This work provides proof-of-concept for a low-cost, portable molecular diagnostic workflow that minimizes infrastructure requirements while maintaining analytical performance.

after.abstract: Elevated plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species are proposed as specific biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology but have also been reported in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Their profile across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases, as well as their discriminatory value when combined with other plasma biomarkers, remain uncertain. We studied 551 participants (ages 40.1 to 87.1 years; 207 women), comprising 506 patients from the Ontario Neurodegenerative Disease Research Initiative (ONDRI) multi-site cohort and 45 amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) PET-negative cognitively unimpaired controls from the Brain-Eye Amyloid Memory study. Ten diagnostic groups were studied: mild cognitive impairment (MCI), AD, Parkinson's disease subdivided into cognitively unimpaired (CU), MCI, and dementia, frontotemporal dementia (FTD), cerebrovascular disease (CVD) subdivided into cognitively unimpaired (CU) and cognitively impaired (CI), ALS, and the control group. Baseline visit plasma measurements included p-tau217, p-tau181, A{beta}42/40, neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). Cross-sectional analyses compared biomarker levels as well as p-tau217-based inference of amyloid positivity status across diagnostic groups. Receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC) analyses ascertained the discriminatory capacity of these biomarkers and ratio combinations. Within the ALS group, baseline biomarker measures were also tested for association against baseline clinical features as well as longitudinal measures of neuropsychological change. P-tau217, p-tau181, GFAP, and NfL differed across groups (all P < 0.001). Compared to controls, p-tau217 was elevated in AD and ALS, p-tau181 and GFAP only in AD, and NfL in ALS and FTD. Inferred amyloid-{beta}; positivity was more probable in MCI, AD, ALS, and cognitively impaired CVD groups compared to controls (all P < 0.05). The p-tau217 to NfL ratio discriminated ALS from AD with an ROC-AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85-0.97) compared to p-tau217 alone at 0.65 (95% CI 0.52-0.76). No ALS clinical or longitudinal association survived correction for multiple comparisons. Elevated p-tau217 and inferred amyloid-{beta}; positivity in ALS provide further evidence that the assay signal is not necessarily specific for AD pathology. However, the use of p-tau217 in combination with NfL provides improved discriminatory power between ALS and AD, supporting the use of plasma biomarker combinations rather than sole reliance on individual plasma biomarkers. Inferred amyloid-{beta}; positivity in cognitively impaired CVD may indicate AD and/or cerebral amyloid angiopathy co-pathology. Currently available plasma biomarkers should therefore be used as diagnostic complements and interpreted within clinical context rather than as standalone molecular diagnoses.

No ALS clinical or longitudinal association survived correction for multiple comparisons. Inferred amyloid-{beta}; positivity in cognitively impaired CVD may indicate AD and/or cerebral amyloid angiopathy co-pathology. Currently available plasma biomarkers should therefore be used as diagnostic complements and interpreted within clinical context rather than as standalone molecular diagnoses.

after.abstract: Background Autonomic symptoms are common in Parkinson disease (PD) and impact quality of life, with unclear relationship to motor and cognitive progression. Objective: Characterize five-year progression of autonomic symptoms in early PD and their association with motor and cognitive outcomes. Methods We analyzed data from 874 PD participants and 252 healthy controls (HC) enrolled in Parkinson Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI). Autonomic symptoms were assessed annually over five years using Scales for Outcomes in Parkinson's disease-Autonomic dysfunction (SCOPA-AUT); affected autonomic domains were defined as domain subscore >1. Clinical measures included MDS-UPDRS and Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Generalized estimating equations evaluated longitudinal changes, adjusting for age, sex, medication, and comorbidities. Results: At baseline, 71% of PD participants reported >1 affected autonomic domain, increasing to 85% among 287 PD participants with 5-year follow-up; HCs reporting >1 affected autonomic domain increased from 40% of participants at baseline to 46% among 145 participants with 5-year follow-up. Gastrointestinal and urinary symptoms were most prevalent in PD. Medication use for constipation and urinary dysfunction increased over time in PD. Cardiovascular comorbidities were common and increased in prevalence in both groups. Greater baseline autonomic symptom burden predicted more rapid cognitive, but not motor decline in PD (p=0.002). Conclusion: Autonomic symptoms in PD are common at disease onset, near universal after 5 years, and associated with faster cognitive, but not motor, decline, driven by those with severe symptoms. The high prevalence and impact of autonomic symptoms in early PD highlights the importance of early assessment and management of these symptoms.

after.abstract: Background. Donepezil, galantamine and rivastigmine are dispensed free of charge to people with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease in the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), but their comparative long-term effectiveness in routine care is unknown. Under the national clinical protocol, memantine is added to a cholinesterase inhibitor (ChEI) when the disease reaches the moderate stage, so memantine add-on can serve as a marker of clinical progression. Methods. Nationwide new-user cohort study emulating a target trial in which adults with Alzheimer's disease eligible for a ChEI would be randomly assigned to start donepezil, galantamine or rivastigmine and followed for memantine add-on. We used outpatient medication dispensing authorizations (APAC records of the Outpatient Information System, SIA/SUS) from all 27 federative units, January 2018 to December 2025. We included patients who started a single ChEI between October 2019, after memantine was first recorded nationally, and December 2025, after at least 12 months without anti-dementia dispensing. The outcome was the first memantine dispensing after the index month. Follow-up ended at add-on, recorded death, loss to follow-up (more than 3 observed months without dispensing) or end of data. Deaths were rarely recorded and were treated as censoring. One pseudonymized health card number shared by many patients was excluded, and follow-up ended earlier in the two affected states. We estimated the risk of add-on at 12 to 48 months had all patients started each drug and remained under observation, using stabilized inverse probability of treatment and censoring weights, with 95% confidence intervals (CI) from 200 bootstrap replicates. The analysis assumed no unmeasured confounding or informative censoring given the measured covariates. Results. The cohort included 142 758 new users (donepezil 74 165; galantamine 30 691; rivastigmine 37 902; mean age 77.3 years; 63.0% women), followed for a median of 14 months; 9 812 memantine add-on events occurred. After weighting, all standardized mean differences were below 0.05. The 24-month weighted cumulative incidence of memantine add-on was 9.7% (95% CI 9.4-10.0) with donepezil, 9.0% (8.6-9.4) with galantamine and 5.6% (5.3-5.9) with rivastigmine. Compared with donepezil, the 24-month risk difference was -0.7 percentage points (pp) (-1.1 to -0.3) for galantamine and -4.1 pp (-4.5 to -3.7) for rivastigmine (risk ratio 0.58, 0.55-0.61). Estimates were stable across sensitivity analyses, including a composite outcome that counted unrecorded deaths and dropouts as events (24-month risk difference -4.1 pp, -4.8 to -3.3) and analyses within age groups (risk ratio 0.64 below 75 years). Deaths were almost never recorded in the dispensing data (at most 0.47% of treated patients per year). Conclusions. In routine SUS care, initiation with rivastigmine, mostly as a transdermal patch, was associated with a lower risk of memantine add-on than initiation with donepezil or galantamine. Because disease severity and death are not recorded in the dispensing data, this difference may reflect prescribing patterns or residual confounding by severity rather than slower progression; additional analyses made differential mortality a less likely explanation. It should be confirmed with linked clinical and mortality data.

after.authors: Badjo, J.-P.; Choa, F.-S.
after.abstract: Sensory gating (SG), most commonly quantified using the auditory P50 event-related potential elicited by a paired "double-click" paradigm, is a well-established biomarker of early sensory inhibition that reflects the brain's ability to suppress responses to repetitive sensory input. Although auditory SG paradigms have been widely used in both research and clinical settings, they impose an unavoidable auditory load and are generally limited to controlled laboratory environments, reducing their suitability for ecological monitoring and applications in which auditory resources must remain available. This study evaluated the feasibility of a portable vibrotactile sensory-gating system designed to assess inhibitory processing without engaging the auditory or visual modalities. Fifteen healthy adult participants completed both auditory and vibrotactile paired-stimulus conditions using a within-subject experimental design. Vibrotactile stimuli were delivered through transducers positioned on the volar surface of the forearm while electroencephalographic (EEG) activity was recorded using a 32-channel Emotiv EPOC Flex system. Event-related responses were extracted and analyzed using conventional sensory-gating metrics to enable direct comparison between modalities. Vibrotactile stimulation elicited time-locked P50 responses with attenuation of S2 relative to S1. Mean S2/S1 ratios were 0.521 +- 0.041 for the auditory condition and 0.524 +- 0.064 for the vibrotactile condition. The paired difference was 0.0029 (95% CI, -0.0221 to 0.0279), t(14) = 0.249, p = 0.807, dz = 0.064. No statistically significant difference was detected between modalities in this sample. These group-level findings support further evaluation of portable vibrotactile P50 measurement.

after.abstract: Background: Brain metastases (BMs), the most common intracranial tumor, do not distribute uniformly throughout the brain, but instead preferentially localize to specific regions. Building on known associations with perfusion and the gray-white matter junction, we hypothesized that regional vulnerability to BMs also reflects the cellular and molecular organization of the healthy brain. Methods: In a discovery cohort of 1,406 patients, we generated a voxelwise map of BM distribution and compared it with normative atlases of brain microstructure, vasculature, metabolism, cell-type composition, and gene expression. Associations were tested for replication in an independent multicenter validation cohort of 1,209 patients. Results: In the discovery cohort, BM frequency was higher near the gray-white matter junction and in regions with greater cerebral perfusion, glucose metabolism, and mitochondrial density. At the cellular level, BM frequency was inversely related to astrocyte and microglial transcriptional signatures. Using normative gene expression maps derived from postmortem healthy brain tissue, we identified 17 genes spatially associated with BM vulnerability and specific to metastases relative to other intracranial lesion types. These associations replicated in the validation cohort. The immune checkpoint gene LAG3 ranked among the ten genes most positively associated with metastatic vulnerability across all genes tested (r = 0.40-0.45, p < 0.001). LAG3 expression was also elevated in peritumoral brain metastasis tissue relative to control brain tissue in an independent spatial transcriptomic dataset. Conclusions: These findings suggest that BM vulnerability reflects healthy brain organization and identify LAG-3, a clinically targetable immune checkpoint, as a candidate link between regional brain immune biology and metastatic colonization.

after.abstract: MGMT promoter (MGMTp) methylation is a clinically important epigenetic biomarker that guides therapeutic decision-making in patients with glioblastoma and related brain malignancies. Pyrosequencing is a widely used method for analysis of MGMTp methylation in molecular pathology laboratories which relies on chemical conversion of DNA prior to amplification by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and subsequent sequencing. The EpiDirect technology represents a novel analytical approach that enables direct, quantitative assessment of DNA methylation by qPCR using native, unmodified DNA. Here we compared the EpiDirect MGMT Methylation qPCR Assay to MGMTp pyrosequencing using brain tumor samples to evaluate the correlation between the two methods. We show that there is a clear correlation across two different clinical cohorts involving both formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) and fresh frozen samples and show that the EpiDirect MGMT Methylation qPCR Assay is a valid alternative to pyrosequencing for quantitative assessment of MGMTp methylation in brain cancer samples.

after.authors: Garcia, C.; Guerit, F.; Arzounian, D.; Carlyon, R. P.
after.abstract: Purpose: We investigated the mechanisms behind the generation of Neural Distortion Responses (NDRs) measured with electroencephalography when interleaving amplitude-modulated (AM) pulse trains in cochlear implant (CI) users. Methods: Previous experiments measured NDRs using interleaved pulse trains in which odd- and even-numbered pulses were respectively modulated at F1 and F2 Hz, where F1=2*F2/3 and F1{approx}80Hz. Experiment 1 separated quadratic and cubic distortion products using a relationship of F1 and F2 such that F1 = (2*F2/3)+2. Experiment 2 retained the original F1=2*F2/3 relationship but shifted the starting AM phase of F2 relative to that of F1. Experiment 3 simultaneously separated the quadratic and cubic distortion products and varied the relative phase of F1 and F2. Experiment 4 flipped the leading polarity of the second pulse in each pulse-pair such that the central phase of the resulting pseudo-triphasic pulses was anodic. All experiments were conducted with Cochlear CI users and interpreted using two computational models of the electrically stimulated auditory nerve. Results: Both quadratic (QDR) and cubic distortion products (CDR) were observed. Varying relative AM phase had an effect on NDR amplitudes, with the largest amplitude when maxima of the 2 AM patterns were aligned. Stimulating with an anodic central phase within the AM pulse pairs resulted in stronger responses for 4 of 9 CI users. Computational modelling suggested a stronger role for refractoriness than for facilitation in generating the NDR, but failed to fully account for the effect of flipping the polarity. Conclusion: NDRs consist of both quadratic and cubic components, and are greatest when maxima of the F1 and F2 pulse trains align. Refractoriness is likely more important than facilitation for generating the NDR.

after.abstract: Polygenic prediction of depression is limited by the depth of depression phenotyping available at biobank scale as well as sample size. Here we develop a depression score combining information from depression and genetically correlated psychiatric traits using phenotype reconstruction, multi-trait genetic integration and Bayesian effect estimation. Compared with the strongest publicly available depression-only score (Psychiatric Genomics Consortium 2025, excluding 23andMe), the liability-R2 for depression in UK Biobank rose by 49.7% and within-family standardized associations with latent internalizing were up to 54% larger. Across 2,328 childhood and adolescent outcomes in the ABCD study, the association profile of the integrated score was almost identical to that of the depression-only score (r = 0.99), while being uniformly stronger. 1,494 outcomes related to mood, behavior, social functioning, hobbies and sleep were associated with the score -- 423 of them within-family. In ABCD, adolescents in the highest score decile were 3.5 times as likely as those in the lowest decile to report suicidal thoughts by age 14 (23% versus 7%) and 1.9 times as likely to report nicotine or cannabis use by age 17 (47% versus 25%). In adults, the score predicted worse general health, chronic pain, and life dissatisfaction. Associations with psychiatric symptoms were substantially stronger in girls than in boys (boys' coefficients 0.68 times girls'), particularly for girl-typical symptoms, and showed no moderation by household resources, hardship or deprivation that remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Prediction was attenuated in line with genetic distance from training data for Hispanic and African American children. Depression prediction can thus be strengthened substantially by integrating the internalizing spectrum, without detectable loss of specificity or within-family predictive ability.

Here we develop a depression score combining information from depression and genetically correlated psychiatric traits using phenotype reconstruction, multi-trait genetic integration and Bayesian effect estimation. Compared with the strongest publicly available depression-only score (Psychiatric Genomics Consortium 2025, excluding 23andMe), the liability-R2 for depression in UK Biobank rose by 49.7% and within-family standardized associations with latent internalizing were up to 54% larger. Across 2,328 childhood and adolescent outcomes in the ABCD study, the association profile of the integrated score was almost identical to that of the depression-only score (r = 0.99), while being uniformly stronger. 1,494 outcomes related to mood, behavior, social functioning, hobbies and sleep were associated with the score -- 423 of them within-family. In ABCD, adolescents in the highest score decile were 3.5 times as likely as those in the lowest decile to report suicidal thoughts by age 14 (23% versus 7%) and 1.9 times as likely to report nicotine or cannabis use by age 17 (47% versus 25%). In adults, the score predicted worse general health, chronic pain, and life dissatisfaction. Associations with psychiatric symptoms were substantially stronger in girls than in boys (boys' coefficients 0.68 times girls'), particularly for girl-typical symptoms, and showed no moderation by household resources, hardship or deprivation that remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Prediction was attenuated in line with genetic distance from training data for Hispanic and African American children. Depression prediction can thus be strengthened substantially by integrating the internalizing spectrum, without detectable loss of specificity or within-family predictive ability.

after.title: Preprint: Functional analysis enables reclassification of SCN1A missense variants of uncertain significance in epilepsy
after.authors: Pilli, K.; Allan, T. J.; Bennett, M. F.; Harris, R. V.; Schneider, A. L.; Shen, Q.; Ma, J. G.; Hildebrand, M. S.; Palmer, E. E.; George, A. L.; Berkovic, S. F.; Vandenberg, J. I.; Scheffer, I. E.; Ng, C.-A.
after.abstract: SCN1A, the most prominent gene for epilepsy, encodes the pore-forming subunit of the voltage-gated sodium channel, NaV1.1. Loss-of-function variants reduce NaV1.1 activity in inhibitory neurons leading to hyperexcitability; they are associated with a spectrum of epilepsies, from self-limited phenotypes in genetic epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, to the prototypic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, Dravet syndrome. Thousands of SCN1A missense variants have been identified, but determining pathogenicity using ACMG criteria can be challenging. Currently, 48% of missense SCN1A variants in ClinVar are classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS). We aimed to provide functional evidence to inform variant classification using a high-throughput automated patch-clamp assay. We validated our assay using 27 true pathogenic SCN1A variants and 25 true benign variants. The results show that 17/27 true pathogenic variants from patients with Dravet syndrome showed severe reductions in current density, precluding gating analysis. Of the remaining ten true pathogenic variants, seven showed an increased voltage difference between the midpoints of activation and inactivation (V0.5diff). Current density and V0.5diff were combined within a graded Bayesian framework to derive a functional log-likelihood ratio reflecting the magnitude of loss of function. We then applied our validated assay to 16 SCN1A missense variants detected in an Australian cohort: three likely pathogenic, one likely benign and 12 VUSs. These variants occurred in 31 individuals from 16 families with a broad phenotypic spectrum, including four individuals with Dravet syndrome who carried p.Ser243Phe, p.Met973Val or p.Lys1911Glu. All three variants showed loss of function: p.Ser243Phe had reduced current density, whereas p.Met973Val and p.Lys1911Glu had abnormal V0.5diff despite current density within the normal range. Of these 16 variants, ten have combined functional scores consistent with abnormal functional evidence. Combining our functional evidence with ACMG criteria, our findings changed the classification of eight of 16 variants (50%), with six of 12 VUS reclassified as likely pathogenic and two of three likely pathogenic variants upgraded to pathogenic. We show that calibrated automated patch-clamp assays can provide actionable functional data to enable the interpretation and reclassification of SCN1A variants and inform clinical care, allowing therapeutic optimisation and facilitating access to genetic therapies.

after.authors: Keating, N.; Mesdaghi, M.; Chavoshzadeh, Z.; Karimi, A.; Saberi, M.; Unal, S.; Meynier, V.; Soudee, C.; Laine, C.; Solgi, A.; Sharafian, S.; LHonneur, A.-S.; Migaud, M.; Seeleuthner, Y.; Cobat, A.; Abel, L.; Beziat, V.; Rosain, J.; Bustamante, J.; Casanova, J.-L.; Boisson-Dupuis, S.

after.abstract: Two otherwise healthy patients from Colombia, now aged 30 and 38 years, developed pulmonary tuberculosis due to inherited, complete TNF deficiency at the ages of 19 and 18 years. We report here a previously healthy Iranian patient with inherited complete TNF deficiency who was diagnosed with both pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB between 10 and 15 years of age. The homozygous TNF variant (c.673C>T) introduces a premature stop codon (TNF p.Q225*) resulting in losses of expression and function. Despite normal myeloid and lymphoid subset development, the patient's primary leukocytes do not secrete detectable amounts of TNF. As in the TNF-deficient Colombian patients, the respiratory burst of GM-CSF-derived macrophages is impaired. Our findings expand the spectrum of TB phenotypes in patients with TNF deficiency and confirm that TNF is essential for immunity to M. tuberculosis in humans but apparently redundant against many other pathogens, including weakly virulent mycobacteria.

after.title: Preprint: Improving Consistency in Colorectal Cancer Genetic Risk Assessment and Return of Results Through an Integrated Polygenic Risk Score
after.authors: Tran, H.; Mulford, A. J.; Wei, J.; Shi, Z.; Ashworth, A.; Zheng, S. L.; Helfand, B. T.; Hulick, P. J.; DePersia, A.; Suh, G.; Jones, B.; Sanders, A. R.; Xu, J.
after.abstract: Background: Published colorectal cancer (CRC) polygenic risk scores (PRS) may demonstrate similar population-level predictive performance but often assign substantially different risk classifications to the same individuals. Such discordance presents challenges for clinical implementation and return of results (RoR). Methods: We developed a stable PRS for CRC (stPRS-CRC) by integrating 28 published PRS using PRSmix in the All of Us (AoU) development cohort (n=321,703). Performance was evaluated in a held-out AoU validation cohort (n=80,423) and independently validated in the Genomic Health Initiative (GHI) (n=17,545). CRC associations were assessed using logistic regression, comparing individuals in the highest PRS decile with the remaining 90%. Individual-level concordance in high-risk classification was evaluated using mean Jaccard indices. Results: Published CRC PRS showed substantial discordance in individual-level high-risk classification despite generally consistent associations with CRC. stPRS-CRC integrated information from multiple published PRS and demonstrated CRC associations comparable to PGS003852, the strongest-performing individual PRS. The odds ratios for stPRS-CRC were 1.94 (95% CI, 1.79-2.11) in AoU development, 2.08 (1.76-2.45) in AoU validation, and 2.08 (1.55-2.79) in GHI. Mean Jaccard indices using stPRS-CRC versus PGS003852 as anchors, each compared with the same 27 published PRS, were 0.29 versus 0.20, 0.43 versus 0.25, and 0.27 versus 0.19, respectively (all P<0.001). Conclusions: Integrating multiple published CRC PRS significantly improved individual-level concordance in high-risk classification while maintaining population-level predictive performance. stPRS-CRC may provide a more consistent framework for clinical genetic risk assessment and ROR.
